item.title: 'I'm really disappointed': Matthew Hayden takes aim at 2018 Australian side over Sandpapergate
item.description: Former Australia opener Matthew Hayden has expressed his disappointment with the 2018 Australian side over the infamous Sandpapergate controversy, saying the team failed to uphold one of the defining characteristics of its cricketing culture – confronting problems collectively inside the dressing room. With the ball-tampering scandal back in the spotlight following fresh revelations by former Australia batter Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft, Hayden believes the focus will eventually shift back to cricket, with Australia having several important assignments ahead, including the Border-Gavaskar Trophy (BGT) in India from January 21, 2027. However, while backing Australia's competitive spirit and its traditional winning culture, Hayden was particularly critical of the players involved in the 2018 episode for not resolving the matter internally. "Will Australia want to win? That's my first question. I can, hand on heart, tell you that Australia will not only be competitive, but will also want to win. In the context of cricket, Australia has largely been very fair in the way it has gone about its cricketing culture. Very little has disrupted the nature of the Australian winning culture. It's a very in-your-face culture. It will confront issues inside the change room collectively. That's why I'm really disappointed in this 2018 mob that couldn't do it," Hayden said on JioStar. Hayden backs Cummins' handling of controversy Hayden also praised current Australia captain Pat Cummins for addressing the renewed questions surrounding the scandal head-on, describing his willingness to face scrutiny and present his version of events as a position of strength. Cummins had dismissed Khawaja's allegations as "utter nonsense" during a press conference, insisting that the bowling group was unaware of the ball-tampering plan. His comments subsequently triggered another round of debate, with Bancroft publishing a lengthy column in The West Australian. Hayden, however, feels the game has largely moved on from the controversy and that the focus will soon return to performances on the field. "Largely, the game has already moved on. Pat Cummins, as you can see, is very keen to embrace his leadership style. He came out with an hour-and-a-bit press conference and said, 'Guys, this is what I've got to say. Ask me any question you want. Challenge me? Sure. Then I'm telling you this is my account of it.' That position is one of strength, and the game has moved on and will move on very quickly. The cricket will speak for itself, and it will speak volumes," he added. Sandpapergate resurfaces ahead of busy Australia schedule The controversy has returned to the headlines after Khawaja, in his autobiography Sabr, claimed that every member of the Australian squad knew about the use of sandpaper during the infamous 2018 South Africa tour. Cummins rejected the allegation, prompting Bancroft, who was caught on television cameras using sandpaper during the Cape Town Test, to revisit

item.title: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta sends blunt reality check to struggling loanee Ethan Nwaneri ahead of Borussia Dortmund Champions League reunion
item.description: Borussia Dortmund v SV Werder Bremen - DFB Cup 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has laid down the law to teenage sensation Ethan Nwaneri as the Gunners prepare to welcome Borussia Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium. The academy graduate moved to the Bundesliga on loan to gain senior experience, but his parent club manager insists that the playmaker’s reputation counts for little in Germany. Arteta delivers harsh reality check to Nwaneri As the north London giants prepare for a pivotal Champions League encounter , the status of Nwaneri has taken centre stage. The youngster is currently spending the campaign at Dortmund , but after a bright start in yellow and black, his minutes have recently dwindled. Arteta was quick to point out that playing for a club of Arsenal's stature does not entitle a player to a starting spot elsewhere, especially at the top of the German top flight. "Well, as you say, he started playing quite a lot, especially starting games, even though he didn't finish many games. Now, recently, he hasn't played that much. He needs to earn the right to play. He's playing at the top of the Bundesliga and the players have huge talent and quality and they are showing that and that's the reality of football," the Spaniard said. The gaffer challenges Nwaneri to prove himself Arteta further added that Nwaneri has the mindset to reveal himself and reclaim his place in the side. He noted that coming from a Premier League heavyweight provides no inherent advantage in a competitive environment like Dortmund’s. The manager is looking for the teenager to show the necessary quality to "earn the right to win" during the remainder of his temporary stint away from the Emirates. "You go there and because you come from Arsenal, it doesn't give you any advantage, so you need to earn it. Ethan has, first of all, the mindset to do it and then the quality to do it and these things are part of a journey and part of a season and he needs to reveal himself and earn the right to win," he stated. David Raya injury update Aside from the loan watch, Arsenal are dealing with a significant blow in goal after David Raya was ruled out of the midweek European clash . The Spanish international suffered a worrying injury recently, and while the initial signs are more positive than first feared, he will not be available to face the Bundesliga leaders. Arteta admitted the club were initially concerned the goalkeeper might require a long-term spell on the sidelines. "He’s not fit for tomorrow, unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than what we expected," Arteta explained. item.title: Jalen Hurts demands a trade from Philadelphia Eagles viral rumour explained
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images A viral rumour claims Jalen Hurts has demanded a trade away from the Philadelphia Eagles. Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts’ 2026-27 NFL season came to an abrupt end after he was diagnosed with blood clots. Initially, Hurts’ condition wasn’t taken seriously, but he’s currently on blood thinners while the NFL is reportedly investigating the Eagles’ medical team for any wrongdoing. Amid this, a Philadelphia reporter has claimed that Hurts has demanded a trade from the Eagles. Jalen Hurts demanding a trade from the Philadelphia Eagles is fake The rumour was started on X by Justin Cohn, who claims that he also broke the news about LeBron James joining the Philadelphia 76ers earlier in the year before anyone else. “Philadelphia Eagles QB Jalen Hurts has informed the team he is requesting a trade. A big reason is Jalen has been unhappy with the way the Eagles handled his injury,” Cohn wrote on X . They added, “The reigning Super Bowl MVP’s time is up in Philadelphia and will be on a new team, barring he can continue to play football.” The report seems fake for a plethora of reasons. First, no major media outlet or insider has backed Cohn’s claim. Second, he claimed that Hurts is the reigning Super Bowl MVP, when the Eagles didn’t even play in it. On the basis of the available information right now, it’s safe to say that Cohn’s claim of Hurts’ trade request is completely baseless and false. Instead, the Eagles QB is likely focused on recovery and returning to the football field sooner rather than later. item.title: Cole Palmer’s Form: Is The Chelsea Number 10 Still Undroppable?
item.description: At various points last season, Cole Palmer’s form was considered one of the major reasons behind Chelsea’s disappointing campaign. While some supporters rightly attributed the club’s 10th-place finish to Enzo Maresca’s departure midway through the season, others believed that the club would have achieved much more had their star player remained fit. Palmer struggled with a persistent groin injury for much of the campaign, limiting his influence when the team needed him most. However, this season, Chelsea supporters have begun asking some uncomfortable questions about the Englishman. Having recovered from his injury and having missed the 2026 World Cup, many expected the Chelsea number 10 to have sufficient time to rest, recover and rediscover his best form. Indeed, the beginning of the campaign suggested that the “ice-man” was ready to replicate his impressive 2023/24 Premier League numbers, as he recorded five goal contributions in his first six league appearances. Since then, however, his performances have taken a worrying downturn. Palmer has managed just one goal in his last five league appearances, with several displays leaving him looking almost invisible on the pitch. This has understandably frustrated supporters who expect considerably more from a player regarded as the creative heartbeat of Chelsea’s attack. At Stamford Bridge, reputation and past achievements can only buy a player so much patience. Palmer remains one of the club’s most talented players, but his recent performances have raised legitimate questions about his consistency, his influence on the team’s attacking play and whether he should retain his automatic starting position. Cole Palmer’s Form: Why Chelsea Fans Are Beginning To Question His Undroppable Status Chelsea’s 4–1 defeat to Leeds United at Stamford Bridge , their first home defeat to the Yorkshire club in 27 years, was embarrassing enough. The team’s overall display, particularly given the historical rivalry between both sides, sparked an extraordinary backlash from Chelsea supporters on social media over the weekend. Despite previous calls from sections of the fanbase to give Xabi Alonso time to implement his ideas and establish his preferred style of play, that patience appears to be running out. Supporters are now demanding the sale of several players they believe are not fighting hard enough for the badge. The Chelsea defence has attracted particular criticism, with fans accusing several players of being too weak and easily bullied by Leeds’ attackers. French defender Wesley Fofana has been among the biggest targets , with some supporters already calling for his immediate departure in the upcoming January transfer window. However, the frustration extends beyond the defence. Questions are being raised about the overall quality, mentality and commitment of the squad, with Chelsea’s disappointing league form suggesting that significant improvements are needed across the pitch. item.title: Conor McGregor ‘gearing up for camp’ in latest gym update before final UFC fight
item.description: Conor McGregor has provided a positive update around his return to the UFC , as he prepares for one last fight . The former champion last competed in July, suffering a torn ACL and meniscus in the opening seconds of his fight with Max Holloway – McGregor’s first bout in five years. The contest was the penultimate fight on McGregor’s contract, and he recently said he intends to fight out his UFC deal with a trilogy clash against Holloway , whom he outpointed in 2013. Conor McGregor after injuring his knee against Max Holloway in July (Getty) In his latest update, the Irishman wrote on Instagram: “Fully back in the gym. Leg presses, deadlifts, loading up the knee and building serious power. “Knee is primed, strength is returning, and the body is firing on all cylinders. “Gearing up for camp. The Notorious is coming.” McGregor’s fight with Holloway this summer was his first since suffering a broken leg in his previous bout, a first-round loss to Dustin Poirier in 2021. It was also the 38-year-old’s first fight since a civil jury found him liable for sexual assault in 2024. McGregor appealed the verdict, which related to an alleged incident in 2018, but his appeal failed. He continues to deny all allegations against him. McGregor is without a win in the UFC since 2020, when he stopped Donald Cerrone in 40 seconds. Since then he has fought just three times, suffering a knockout by Poirier in January 2021 before breaking his leg in their next meeting, six months later. Then came his rematch with Holloway. McGregor collapsed against Holloway due to his knee injury (Getty) McGregor injured himself while trying a running, jumping kick. Curiously, he also injured his knee in his 2013 fight with Holloway, before both fighters went on to become world champions. Holloway, 34, has not fought since his summer clash with McGregor, and the Hawaiian has suggested that he could wait for the Irishman’s return.

item.title: Report card from Nebraska’s triumphant win over No. 14 Ohio State
item.description: Nebraska football pulled off a long-awaited win this past weekend, taking down No. 14 Ohio State , 31-28. This marked the Huskers’ first top 25 win since 2016 and their first win over the Buckeyes since 2011. Nebraska also managed to close out the win after letting multiple contests slip through its fingers not just this season, but in numerous seasons before it. The offense played arguably its most complete game yet, and the defense managed to do just enough to keep Ohio State at bay. However, that doesn’t mean this game was flawless by any means. Here is the report card from Nebraska’s triumphant win over No. 14 Ohio State. Quarterback: A- Anthony Colandrea played his best game of the season, putting the game on his back at just the right moments and guiding the offense to its second straight 31-point outing. But most importantly, he played mostly mistake-free. He tallied 263 total yards and four touchdowns. Colandrea finished 19-of-28 for 200 yards and three touchdowns in the air, hitting his receivers at clutch moments. On the ground, he picked up 63 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, coming through on some of the biggest plays of, not just the game, but arguably of the season. However, while these plays were massive, they don’t fully overshadow the few moments of terror that unfolded in the game. Colandrea still missed a number of throws, some dangerously close to being in harm’s way. He also just avoided putting the ball on the ground on two separate runs, getting a knee or forearm down in the nick of time. In past games, those close calls didn’t go Nebraska’s way. But such moments shouldn’t happen at all. Though the weather made things challenging at times, Colandrea still needs to protect the ball. With Iowa and the bowl game left on the docket, he may not be so lucky. Running Backs: A- Jamal Rule and Isaiah Mozee helped the Huskers control the clock, combining for 31 carries. The result was 113 rushing yards. Rule carried the load, totaling 23 carries. He fought for his yardage, finishing with 70 yards after delivering some firm hits. However, his physicality did result in a blindside block penalty. Mozee, meanwhile, only got eight carries, but broke out two runs of over 10 yards. He finished with 43 yards on the ground. The duo also picked up yardage in the air, combining for 24 yards on three catches. But though the duo did a lot to help Nebraska control the game, nothing spectacular happened. Mekhi Nelson also didn’t even see the field, despite being responsible for two touchdowns across the last couple of weeks. This group did enough nonetheless to win here. But in these final two games of the season, the running backs need to do more damage. Wide Receivers: A- Colandrea found three different receivers for touchdowns in the win. Kwazi Gilmer, Luke Lindenmeyer and Quinn Clark all picked up major scoring plays and helped the Huskers cap off drives, with the team finishing 4-of-4 in the red zone. The trio also combined for 13

item.title: Grandmaster clash: World Chess enters record books as Gen Z contenders fight for title
item.description: Two titans of Chess go head-to-head in Geneva on Tuesday in a match that will be the most youthful world championship contest in the competition's 140-year history. Defending the crown is India's Dommaraju Gukesh, who entered the record books in 2024, when he took the title at 18-years old. He's up against Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan, who's also 20, and for some is favourite to win based on form, having won the World Cup and Candidates Tournament. He's currently fourth in the global rankings compared to Gukesh, who's dropped to 26th. Sindarov also goes into the battle with a psychological advantage with two victories and one draw from their three previous encounters. But, at the press conference on Sunday at the United Nations’ European headquarters where both players presented themselves to the world, Gukesh rejected suggestions that he faced a more difficult task this time round to protect his title. “I don’t think I’m here to defend anything,” he said. “I’m here to win it all over again. That’s the mindset I’m in.” Related The incredible hidden details you missed in Ronaldo and Messi's viral chess photo FILE: The trophy of World Championship 2026 is seen during the opening ceremony of the FIDE World Chess Championship, 22 November 2026 - Salvatore Di Nolfi/Keystone via AP The tournament is taking place at the Fondation Martin Bodmer at Cologny, one of the most important private libraries in the world, as it includes some of the oldest surviving copies of the New Testament and Shakespeare's First Folio from 1623. The match will consist of 14 classical games. The first player to score 7.5 points or more will be crowned World Champion and claim the larger share of the total prize fund of $2.5 million. If the score is equal after 14 games, the winner will be decided by a tiebreak which will be played on 12 December.

item.title: InferNode gives Bell Labs' Inferno OS a 64-bit second wind
item.description: InferNode brings a modernized, 64-bit edition of Inferno, the distributed operating system that followed Plan 9 from Bell Labs. For us, the strapline of the InferNode project distracts from the interesting part. It describes the project as a "Secure Runtime for AI Agents," but we think it's something far more interesting than another LLM tool. Fair warning: this vulture has no interest whatsoever in AI agents, and we are not even going to look at this planned use of InferNode. We're interested in the OS, and here, its GitHub repository spells out the part that caught our attention: "a 64-bit Inferno® OS." That grabbed us because Inferno is a very interesting OS, although it doesn't get much attention – for example, the official Inferno GitHub repository shows little activity in the last few years. Inferno is the successor to Plan 9, which we've written and talked about before , including recent releases of its community continuation, 9front . Plan 9 is what the team who invented Unix did next. Plan 9 is a very minimalist, natively clustered Unix: machines can freely mount one another's filesystems, display windows on one another, and start processes on one another. Plan 9 turns a network of machines running this Unix-like OS into a single machine. So, for instance, if you were working on a laptop with limited storage and compute power, you could compile a large complex project on a faster machine elsewhere on the network, using project files located on a third machine, while watching the process in your terminal on your screen, with no messing about with SSH sessions. Plan 9 and 9front programs are compiled into architecture-specific native binaries. Different processor families can still work together across the network, but the same executable won't run unchanged on both an x86-64 laptop and an Arm64 server. Inferno takes a different approach. It's contemporaneous with the far less ambitious Java. On Inferno, languages compile code for a VM called Dis, which is part of the kernel. This means that Inferno binaries execute directly on anything that the Inferno kernel runs on. The OS kernel is built to run bare-metal, or as a process on various other OSes, without needing a separate hardware virtual machine or hypervisor. A single binary can run on all supported CPU architectures. Inferno applications are normally written in the Limbo programming language , whose documentation was written by Unix co-creator Dennis Ritchie. Limbo is one of the languages that influenced Go, but Inferno lets compilers for other languages target Dis as well. The binaries run anywhere. Inferno on Arm, or x86, or RISC-V, or running in a Windows or Linux or macOS process, your program just runs. We've been trying to contact Vita Nuova , the company that maintains Inferno, for some years without success. Development appears to have slowed considerably. item.title: Mobile Entertainment Growth Raises Fresh Questions About Consumer Safety in Nigeria
item.description: Mobile-first entertainment has become part of everyday life for many Nigerians. A phone can now be a cinema screen, a music player, a social space and, for adults, a gateway to real-money gaming platforms. That convenience is precisely why consumer safety deserves more attention. The shift is not simply about more people using smartphones. It is about how quickly an app, browser page or payment prompt can move someone from browsing to registering, sharing personal information and making a transaction. A few taps may feel routine, but the choices behind them are not always straightforward. For adult users, the sensible question is not just whether a platform looks polished or loads quickly. It is whether the operator is appropriate for their location, whether its rules are clear, how it handles personal data and what controls exist when someone wants to pause or limit their activity. Consumer protection needs to keep pace with the format. Mobile access removes much of the friction that once came with visiting a physical venue, which makes plain information, proper age checks and visible responsible-play tools more important than ever. Nigeria’s mobile reality brings its own questions Nigeria’s digital economy is shaped by mobile use. For many people, a handset is the main route to the internet, rather than a laptop or desktop computer. That puts entertainment, communication, payments and advertising in the same small screen space. It also means conditions vary enormously. Data costs, connection quality, device storage and payment options can differ from one user to the next. A platform that appears simple in a promotional post may involve lengthy terms, automatic settings or data collection that are less obvious on a small display. Digital payments have evolved quickly too. Bank transfers, USSD options, cards and wallet-based services have made online transactions familiar to many adults. Familiarity can be useful, but it can also encourage people to skim past details they would otherwise read. A few consumer questions are worth keeping in mind: Is the service clearly intended for adults aged 18 and over? Is the platform permitted to operate for users in Nigeria or the relevant state? Does it show the operator’s identity, licensing information and contact details? Are payment, withdrawal, identity-check and account-closure rules easy to find? Does the site explain what personal data it collects and why? Age boundaries deserve particular care. Gaming promotion should not be designed to appeal to under-18s, and adult platforms should have meaningful age-gating rather than a token tick-box. Adults with younger people in their household may also want to use device controls and keep account credentials private. Regulation can involve federal and state-level considerations, so broad claims about legality should always be treated cautiously. item.title: Enoch Adeagbo Was Denied Admission for Being Too Young. At 19, He’s Set to Graduate with First-Class Honours
item.description: My name is Enoch Adeagbo. In 2021, at the age of 14, I was refused admission because I was too young. I was very sad because the reason had nothing to do with my academic ability. My parents encouraged me to apply to another university, and I eventually gained admission to Ajayi Crowther University (ACU), Oyo, at the age of 14. On Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at 19, I will graduate from ACU with First Class Honours in Civil Engineering, having earned a CGPA of 4.79 out of 5.00, as the second-best student in my department and the third-best student in the Faculty of Engineering. If I had given up and not applied to another school, I might not be here today sharing my journey. Where it all began As a child, I often accompanied my father to construction sites. I enjoyed watching structures take shape from foundation stage to completion. My interest in how buildings were designed and constructed gradually developed into a desire to become an engineer. At 14, however, I was considerably younger than most of my course mates. People frequently reminded me of my age, and I had to adjust. I learnt to focus on my studies, take part in university activities and make the most of the opportunity I had been given. In the 2022/2023 session, at 15, I received the Overall Best Student in Engineering of the Year award at the 200-level. I had not expected it, but it was also an encouraging recognition of my work, and it motivated me to stay consistent. The C that taught me something But being interested in a course does not necessarily mean you’d understand it completely. I learnt this in the first semester of 400 level, when I got a C in Structural Analysis, a three-unit course I thought I understood. I was surprised because I had been confident in my knowledge of the course. That experience made me reflect on my approach to studying. I became more deliberate about understanding concepts rather than simply assuming I had mastered them. Studying with a group and teaching my coursemates also became valuable. Explaining a topic to someone else also helped me understand the course more. More than lectures Beyond the classroom, I served as the Academic Officer of the Nigerian Universities Engineering Students’ Association (NUESA), ACU Chapter, for the 2025/2026 session. I also served as an Assistant Class Representative and was involved in chapel activities as a chapel worker. My faith in God has played an important role throughout my university journey. It shaped my discipline, decisions and priorities, and helped me remain intentional about my responsibilities. I am grateful to my parents, who made sure I did not have to worry about finances while pursuing my education. Their support allowed me to concentrate on my studies and other responsibilities without the additional burden of financial concerns. item.title: Questions Linger After Jensen Huang’s Return To Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang’s surprise return to Nvidia on Monday appeared to stabilize the US chip giant, along with the broader stock market and AI ecosystem, but questions linger about the longterm impact of his scandal. Is Nvidia in the clear? An internal investigation overseen by independent directors is still underway at Nvidia regarding concerns that Huang might have been the target of an espionage campaign by China. US government officials, including President Donald Trump, assured Nvidia’s board that reinstating the company’s cofounder “poses no national security risk.” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (R) speaks alongside US President Donald Trump about investing in America, at the White House in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo by JIM WATSON / AFP In parallel, the US Department of Justice is investigating Megaspeed, a company based in Singapore that allegedly bought processors from Nvidia and routed them to Chinese customers, circumventing US export restrictions. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has also reportedly launched an investigation into Nvidia’s accounting practices and potentially misleading communication to shareholders. However, the Trump administration has generally avoided going after its allies, so the federal probes might not result in much, Columbia University Professor Eric Talley said. Will Huang be held accountable? Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks during Nvidia Live at CES 2026 ahead of the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 5, 2026. The embattled chief will nevertheless have to explain himself to lawmakers at a closed-door hearing on December 1 before three House committees. He will also testify before a Senate committee on December 3 in a hearing that will be livestreamed, while California’s attorney general has opened an investigation into the company’s chip exports and shareholder disclosures. There are plenty of regulators who are willing to push back against the Trump administration and ask tough questions, Talley said. Trump is also known to flip on people whom he no longer considers friends. “He can become estranged with people, and if that would happen with Jensen Huang, I can imagine a boomerang” on the Trump administration’s approach, Talley said. What does the board’s future look like? The logo of Nvidia is seen during a production preview exhibition in Taipei on May 21, 2025. Photo by I-HWA CHENG / AFP Openly opposed to Huang’s return before ultimately reinstating him, the board is in a delicate position. Former Goldman Sachs chief Lloyd Blankfein predicts its days may be numbered. A revolt by shareholders, many of whom supported the reinstatement of the 63-year-old entrepreneur, could reshape the board as soon as 2027, since all directors stand for reappointment every year. If they are spared, the directors could keep Huang on a much “shorter leash” compared to its history of largely deferring to the overwhelming power of this extraordinary executive, Talley said.

item.title: Champions League: Lookman ruled out of Atletico clash, Osimhen’s return uncertain
item.description: Nigerian forward Ademola Lookman has been ruled out of Atletico Madrid’s UEFA Champions League clash against Viking FK, while Victor Osimhen remains doubtful for Galatasaray’s encounter with Aston Villa. The two Super Eagles stars face uncertain fortunes ahead of Matchday Five, with Lookman set to miss Wednesday’s fixture due to injury. According to reports, Lookman will be unavailable when Atletico Madrid face Viking FK on Wednesday, November 25. His absence adds to the Spanish side’s injury concerns, with Marc Pubill and Romero also ruled out. Meanwhile, Osimhen’s availability for Galatasaray’s home encounter against Aston Villa remains uncertain. The striker recently underwent knee surgery after sustaining an injury during Galatasaray’s 2-0 victory over Stuttgart. He resumed individual training on Thursday, November 19, but was not included in the squad for his side’s victory over Samsunspor three days later. His return to action against Aston Villa is therefore not guaranteed. Elsewhere, Moses Usor will be looking to maintain his impressive form for LASK Linz when they travel to face Bodo/Glimt on Tuesday. Samuel Adeniran is expected to lead the attack alongside Usor, who provided an assist in LASK’s hard-fought 2-1 victory over Hartberg on Saturday. LASK currently occupy 16th position with six points and will be hoping to improve their standing with a positive result in Norway. On Wednesday, fellow Nigerians Mubarak Suleiman and Emmanuel Ayaosi are expected to feature when Slavia Prague host Villarreal at the Fortuna Arena. Slavia have endured a difficult campaign, sitting 34th with just one point after four matches. They are yet to record a victory in the competition. Another Nigerian youngster, Christian Nwachukwu, could also feature when Sabah host Spanish giants Barcelona at the Baku Olympic Stadium on Wednesday. The 20-year-old joined the Azerbaijani club from Sheffield United in August and will have an opportunity to test himself against one of Europe’s biggest sides. item.title: Debo Adedayo (Mr Macaroni) Joins the Fellowship of the Royal Society of Arts in the UK
item.description: Debo Adedayo (Mr Macaroni) joins the Fellowship of the Royal Society of Arts following his Master’s degree graduation in London. Photo Credit: Debo Adedayo/Instagram Have you been keeping up with Debo Adedayo lately? Because the Nigerian actor, content creator and activist—popularly known as Mr Macaroni —just added another major feather to his cap. Debo has officially joined the Fellowship of the Royal Society of Arts (RSA), a UK-based institution recognised globally for bringing together changemakers across the arts, social innovation and public life. Sharing the news with his followers, Debo kept his message warm and forward-looking: I am elated to join the Fellowship of the Royal Society of Arts. Looking forward to learning, sharing and collaborating with artists from around the world who are passionate about impacting our society for good. This recognition arrives right on the heels of a busy, rewarding season for the entertainer in London. Earlier this month, Debo graduated with a Master of Arts with Distinction in Performance (Acting) from the Mountview Academy of Theatre Arts, validated by the University of East Anglia, in the United Kingdom. During his postgraduate training at Mountview, he also made his UK stage debut in July, starring as Lord Commander Thomas Fairfax in Howard Brenton’s historical play 55 Days at The Backstage Theatre in Peckham, London. Debo Adedayo brings historical figure Lord Commander Thomas Fairfax to life in James Yeatman’s stage direction of 55 Days at Mountview Academy of Theatre Arts. Photo Credit: Debo Adedayo/Instagram Long before stepping onto the London theatre stage, Debo Adedayo (born Adebowale Babatunde Adedayo ) earned his first degree in Theatre Arts and Film Studies from Redeemer’s University in 2018. Millions first came to love him in 2019 through his satirical comedy skits—creating memorable characters like Daddy Wa and Professor Hard Life—while he has steadily built an acclaimed Nollywood film career alongside his civic advocacy in Nigeria. Debo Adedayo (Mr Macaroni) holds his Master of Arts with Distinction certificate awarded by the University of East Anglia through Mountview Academy of Theatre Arts. UK gov invests in defense startup making virtual training ground for AI
item.description: The British government is investing in a UK-based AI defense startup that aims to train autonomous military systems in virtual environments, in a bid to reduce the country's reliance on overseas technology. Both the Sovereign AI Fund and the National Security Strategic Investment Fund (NSSIF) have contributed to a Series A funding round for Agon Dynamics, said to value the biz at $450 million. This $70 million round takes the total capital raised by the firm to $100 million, following its initial $30 million seed round earlier this year. The government claims this move will help strengthen the UK’s sovereign capabilities when it comes to the use of AI for defense, plus the hope that nurturing native technical know-how converts into industrial strength and greater resilience. But it is not revealing how much cash it has stumped up, claiming such investments are commercially sensitive, although it did say that typical equity amounts obtained from the the Sovereign AI Fund tend to be worth around £1 million to £10 million ($1.3 million to $13 million). Agon is understood to be developing facilities to train and test AI systems needed for defense. This covers systems to help defend against drone attacks, or ensuring that AI tools still continue to work as intended if communications with the command center are disrupted. Training like this currently needs to be carried out in the real world, which is time-consuming and expensive, according to the government. For this reason, Agon is building a "virtual battlefield" environment where AI models can be tested against realistic simulations of the situations they might encounter. The company says its synthetic battle arena provides a safe, repeatable environment for developers and defense contractors to try out autonomous systems against thousands of demanding scenarios before deployment. Systems can face adaptive virtual adversaries informed by live conflict intelligence, helping them to respond to evolving tactics, threats and operating conditions. This may include simulations of mass drone attacks that would overwhelm conventional air defense systems, or testing how autonomous systems operate when navigation is degraded or adversary tactics change. "Europe is in an AI arms race as we enter the era of agentic warfare: intelligent agents and machines that will need to understand their environment, make decisions and adapt at a speed and scale that humans alone cannot match," says co-founder and CEO Tristam Constant, a former British Army officer. "We exist to build the sovereign infrastructure and AI foundation models to allow us to train, test, and evolve autonomous defense systems, in Europe, for Europe - to outperform adversary capabilities." For the government, AI Minister Kanishka Narayan claimed that Britain is well-placed to lead efforts to ensure such technologies are reliable, trustworthy, and deployed responsibly. item.title: Canada PM brings Trump impersonator on stage during press gala
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney invited a Donald Trump impersonator on stage during a weekend press gala, a move one critic said risks provoking a president known to bristle at being mocked. Carney was making a lighthearted speech at the Canadian equivalent of the White House Correspondents’ Dinner when he announced he was pressing an “emergency comedy button.” Comedian Mark McKinney, who impersonates Carney, came out first, followed by Trump impersonator Mark Critch, who appears on the long-running Canadian sketch comedy show “This Hour Has 22 Minutes.” “We’ve got two Carneys here, it’s a disaster,” Critch joked as Trump, before taking shots at Washington’s controversial ambassador to Canada and the White House press secretary vacancy, after Katie Zacharia left the role in just five days. With the United States and Canada still locked in a trade war, Critch offered some comic assurances about an impending pact. “Mark, we’re gonna have an incredible deal,” he said, mimicking Trump. “There’s only one thing standing in the way — me, because I’m crazy.” The bit appeared to go down well with reporters in Ottawa, but one of Carney’s political rivals was unimpressed. “I think provoking President Trump is arrogant, stupid and not funny,” said Yves-Francois Blanchet, the leader of the separatist Bloc Quebecois. He noted that Trump’s tariffs, including those affecting an aluminum industry central to Quebec’s economy, are causing real economic pain. “Quebec is paying the highest price for these tariffs…which should not be inflamed with bad jokes,” Blanchet said. Trump and Carney have both offered optimism that trade talks are progressing, but there were similarly positive comments in the days before negotiations collapsed in August. Canada wants relief from tariffs on key sectors, notably autos, but Ottawa has warned that completely removing the levies is unlikely and the Canadian economy needs to adjust to a permanently altered trading relationship with the United States. The post Canada PM brings Trump impersonator on stage during press gala appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Six killed, several injured in Delta political campaign clash – Police
item.description: The Nigeria Police Force has confirmed that six people died and several others sustained injuries during a violent incident at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The Force also said the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, had ordered a comprehensive investigation into the incident, including the actions of police officers deployed to the venue. CSP Ani Iniedu, the Force Public Relations Officer, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, adding that preliminary police findings indicated that six people were killed. “Preliminary Police reports indicate that six persons lost their lives, while several others sustained injuries. “The Force is aware of varying casualty figures circulating in the public domain. An ongoing investigation will establish the verified number of casualties and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident,” the statement read. Iniedu said the IGP had instructed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation. He added that the probe would examine the sequence of events, establish the identities of those involved and determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the actions and deployment of police personnel at the scene. The Force also confirmed that the Delta State Government had imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, running from 6pm to 6am daily until further notice. “In response to the security situation, the Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, until further notice. The Delta State Police Command is enforcing the directive and has intensified security measures to prevent further breakdown of law and order,” the statement read. The police urged residents, community leaders, political stakeholders and campaign groups to remain peaceful, obey the curfew and refrain from circulating unverified reports that could worsen tensions. It also called on anyone with useful information, photographs, video footage or other evidence to assist the investigation by submitting them through established police channels, assuring that the identity of informants would be protected. The police confirmation followed an earlier allegation by the campaign organisation of former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, that gunmen attacked his entourage during a campaign tour of the area. The organisation had put the death toll at four, including two of its aides, identified as Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro, while claiming that four other people sustained critical injuries. The post Six killed, several injured in Delta political campaign clash – Police appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‎After Daily Trust story, foundation sponsors surgery for Kano teen battling facial tumour
item.description: ‎The Ihsan Scholarship Foundation, Kano, has sponsored the life-changing surgery of Salisu Sani, an 18-year-old whose struggle with a debilitating facial tumour was highlighted by Daily Trust, restoring hope to the teenager and offering him a chance to rebuild his future. ‎‎Daily Trust had reported how Salisu Sani, an indigene of Yalwa town in Tofa Local Government Area of Kano State, spent his days along Gandun Albasa Street in Kano soliciting support for a critical surgery after a massive tumour on his face left him in constant pain and threatened his eyesight. ‎‎Following the publication, a Kano-based foundation known for its humanitarian and educational interventions reached out to the teenager and took over the responsibility of his treatment. ‎The foundation, which requested anonymity, facilitated his return to the [Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital (AKTH), where medical evaluations were conducted and the much-needed surgery was successfully carried out. ‎Medical records obtained by Daily Trust showed that specialists at the hospital diagnosed the condition as Aggressive Trabecular Ossifying Fibroma, a rare fibro-osseous tumour affecting the jaw and facial bones. ‎The pathology report indicated that tissue samples removed during surgery weighed about 640 grams. ‎‎Family members expressed gratitude to the foundation, medical personnel and members of the public who showed concern after the story was published. ‎Speaking after the successful operation, Salisu Sani said the intervention had given him a new lease of life. ‎“I never imagined that help would come this fast. For years I lived with the pain and the burden of carrying this tumour on my face. Today, I feel hopeful again,” he said. ‎The teenager had earlier told Daily Trust that the illness had forced him out of school and shattered his dreams, as his family could not afford the cost of treatment. ‎In a further boost to his recovery and future, the foundation also pledged to support his long-term rehabilitation by either sponsoring his education or providing him with full startup capital to establish a business and become self-reliant. ‎‎A representative of the foundation said the decision was informed by the need to ensure that the teenager not only receives medical care but also has the opportunity to build a productive life after recovery. ‎‎“Our concern is not limited to the surgery alone. We want him to be able to stand on his own feet and pursue his dreams. Whether through formal education or entrepreneurship, we will support him to become self-reliant,” the representative said.

item.title: Education software supplier's legacy login system left 355,000 school email addresses exposed
item.description: More than 355,000 school staff and pupil email addresses ended up in the hands of hackers who broke into UK education software supplier Bromcom in September. The breach was added to Have I Been Pwned on Monday, revealing that 355,051 unique email addresses were caught up in the incident. The data also included single sign-on (SSO) registration reference numbers, although Bromcom insists that no passwords or authentication tokens were stolen. As The Register reported in Octobe r , the attackers got in through a legacy SSO registration component in Bromcom's Communications Server environment. The technology had already been superseded but was still running because an internal system continued to use it. Bromcom discovered something was amiss on September 6 after customers reported problems accessing its SSO service. At the time, the company was still working with external forensic specialists to establish exactly what the intruders had managed to get their hands on. Bromcom's FAQ says its investigation is complete and confirms that the intruders used a script to extract SSO registration information from the compromised server. The supplier insists its Management Information System (MIS), used by schools to keep track of everything from attendance to pupil records, was untouched. The compromised service also couldn't be used to get into Microsoft or Google accounts, which have their own login systems. Bromcom has since pulled the plug on the old component, tightened its authorization checks, and added more security logging. It says it hasn't found any evidence of accounts being hijacked as a result of the breach. Bromcom also confirmed it hadn't reported the breach to the UK's Information Commission's Office. Its reasoning is that it was the data processor, not the controller, so any decision to involve the regulator was for the affected schools and academy trusts to make. As for the risk to staff and pupils, Bromcom considers it to be low. No passwords or pupil records held in the MIS were taken, it says, although schools have been advised to watch for phishing messages and suspicious requests to reset passwords or approve sign-ins. The supplier's software is used by more than 5,000 schools and 390 multi-academy trusts across the UK, though it hasn't said how many were caught up in this particular mess. The Register has asked Bromcom how many schools and pupils were affected, and whether the figure published by Have I Been Pwned matches its own findings, but has yet to receive a response. Bromcom kept the superseded component running because an internal system still needed it. Unfortunately, the intruders found a use for it too. ®

item.title: ‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠⁠​​‌⁠‌INEC to conduct mock accreditation in 490 Lagos polling units
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it will conduct a mock accreditation and result upload exercise in 490 polling units across Lagos State on Saturday. Prof. Ayobami Salami, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Lagos State, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Lagos. Salami said the exercise would take place between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. in selected polling units across the state. He said it was designed to assess the performance of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and identify possible gaps or challenges that would be addressed before the 2027 general elections. According to him, the exercise will cover the 245 Registration Areas (RAs) across the state’s 20 Local Government Areas (LGAs), with two polling units selected in each Registration Area. He urged residents, particularly eligible voters in the selected polling units, to participate in the exercise to enable the commission to assess the effectiveness of its equipment and electoral processes. The REC said the list of selected polling units would be displayed at the respective local government area offices to enable residents to identify the designated locations. Salami said he had directed all electoral officers in the state to convene stakeholder meetings in their respective LGAs ahead of the exercise. He said the meetings would provide an opportunity to engage political parties and other stakeholders on the importance of participating in the mock accreditation exercise. The REC said the engagements would also help mobilise eligible voters in the selected polling units to participate in the exercise. He outlined the activities preceding the exercise, saying BVAS configuration would take place on Nov. 25, followed by the training of nominated personnel on Nov. 26. According to him, personnel and devices would be deployed to the selected polling units on Friday, ahead of the exercise. Salami reiterated that the exercise formed part of INEC’s preparations to ensure a smooth and efficient electoral process during the 2027 general elections. (NAN) The post ‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠⁠​​‌⁠‌INEC to conduct mock accreditation in 490 Lagos polling units appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Woman attacks police inspector, tears uniform during arrest
item.description: By Steve Oko A woman, identified as Ettoh Barkerk, has been arrested by the Abia State Police Command for allegedly assaulting a police inspector and tearing his uniform during a confrontation in Aba. The suspect was also accused of attacking worshippers with fireworks at Christ the King Church (CKC), Aba, triggering panic within the church premises. The police said Barkerk was arrested on Sunday, November 22, after a distress call alerted the Ndiegoro Divisional Police Headquarters to an attack on church members by hoodlums throwing explosive fireworks indiscriminately. According to the Command, a patrol team deployed to the scene to restore order apprehended the suspect with fireworks in her possession. However, she allegedly turned violent, assaulted an inspector attached to the patrol team, tore his uniform and attempted to forcefully retrieve the recovered exhibits. The police said she was subsequently subdued and arrested, while the fireworks and other relevant exhibits were secured for investigation. The Command’s spokesperson, DSP Maureen Chinaka, disclosed this in a statement Monday, condemning the assault as reprehensible and warning against attacks on officers performing lawful duties. She said the suspect would be charged in court after investigation. Chinaka added that normalcy had been restored at the church and its environs, while police monitoring continued to prevent further breakdown of law and order. The Command warned that it would not tolerate assault, obstruction or interference with police officers in the discharge of their duties, urging residents to maintain peace and respect lawful authority. The post Woman attacks police inspector, tears uniform during arrest appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The Design Table 2026 by So.Me Solutions: African Fashion in the Spotlight with $7,000 in Award Support for Emerging Designers
item.description: The Design Table 2026 brought together some of the voices, ideas and creative forces shaping African fashion for an afternoon of industry exchange, recognition and conversation. The annual cultural platform, produced by So.Me Solutions, welcomed designers, fashion entrepreneurs, industry leaders, media personalities and fashion enthusiasts for its latest edition. Held at GRAS Lagos, Victoria Island, during Lagos Fashion Week, this year’s gathering explored the people, perspectives and opportunities influencing the future of African fashion. The event also marked a significant milestone for So.Me Solutions, which celebrates 10 years as a 360 communications agency. Among the guests were Folake Amber (Tiffany Amber), Bola Balogun (Glam Brand), Sharon Adeleke, Beverly Naya, Awed by Moni, Marvy Olugu (House of Marvee) and Funmi Ford , alongside other familiar faces from across fashion, entertainment and the creative scene. A Seat at the Table for the Next Generation A major highlight of this year’s edition was the Next Gen Design Impact Award, which received 101 applications from emerging designers. Following the selection process, three finalists, Sultana, Dimeji Ilori and Bjuv Woman , were shortlisted for the award. The finalists were evaluated by a five-member jury comprising Dr. Yetty Ogunnubi, Odio Mimonet, Eniafe Momodu, Ugonna-Ora Owoh and Yoanna “Pepper”, with guests also participating in the voting process. Bhuv Woman emerged as the winner, receiving the $5,000 grand prize funded by Vlisco, Patrón and Culture Lab. In addition, Odio Mimonet extended a further $2,000 in award support, bringing the total prize support associated with the award to $7,000. Beyond the financial support, the winning package includes mentorship, industry access and opportunities to further advance the designer’s work. The announcement was an emotional moment for Bhuv Woman, who was visibly moved as she received the recognition and expressed gratitude to the organisers. Through the award, The Design Table continues to create opportunities for emerging designers to gain visibility, access and recognition while connecting them with established voices and resources within the fashion industry. Who Gets to Shape the Future of African Fashion? The conversations continued with a speakers session titled “ Who Gets to Shape the Future of African Fashion?” , moderated by Yvan Otu and featured Mai Atafo , founder of ATAFO; Ezinne Chinkata , founder of Zinkata; Sacha Okoh, fashion entrepreneur and creative director of Viva; Kiki Osinbajo , founder of CIAR; and Tess Tanaka, founder of Moda54. The session explored how African fashion can move beyond being treated as a niche category and become more firmly integrated into the wider global fashion landscape. Discussions touched on what it takes for African brands to be stocked, worn and embraced as part of everyday fashion, alongside the realities of production, pricing, distribution, customer experience and access to markets. item.title: YouTube star Ms Rachel protests US child immigration hearings
item.description: Ms Rachel, the American creator of hit sing-songy educational videos for toddlers, attacked the use of immigration hearings for children following a courthouse visit on Monday. “I’ve seen children who are just missing the light in their eyes and they’re begging to go to the spelling bee or to just, you know, be with their younger siblings,” said Ms Rachel, who is known offline as Rachel Accurso. “They’re just so scared and praying to God, that they, please change the hearts of ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement) and let us out,” added the 43-year-old after observing legal procedures of juveniles being processed through the immigration courts. Her appearance at the New York youth immigration court was part of an effort to shine light on the Trump administration’s immigration policy that was supported by newly elected US lawmaker Brad Lander. Lander criticized a “travesty of justice” as cases are sped up while funding for legal representation is cut. In videos uploaded to her 22 million subscribers on YouTube, Ms Rachel, known for her signature pink headband and denim overalls, teaches infants to identify animals, colors, and numbers. On her other social media platforms, she is taking an increasingly vocal stand for children’s rights. She has notably led a fundraiser for the organization Save the Children in support of Palestinian children in Gaza and has backed campaigns critical of US migrant detention centers where children are kept, decrying poor conditions and calling for their closure. Targeted by a smear campaign for her pro-Gaza stance, Ms Rachel said previously that it would be more controversial to say nothing. “I think it’s sad to take someone’s dedication and love for all children and try and make that wrong,” she told PBS last year. The post YouTube star Ms Rachel protests US child immigration hearings appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Paris Club Refunds: Court freezes N135.5bn linked to Governors’ Forum
item.description: …restrains 29 banks By Taiye Agbaje An Abuja High Court has ordered an interim freeze on N135.5 billion paid to the Nigerian Governors’ Forum (NGF) as a stakeholder in the Paris Club refunds dispute. Justice O. C. Agbaza granted the interim Mareva injunction following an ex-parte application brought by Dr Ted Iseghohi-Edwards. The order restrained the Incorporated Trustees of the NGF from withdrawing, transferring, dissipating or otherwise dealing with the funds. The order also restrained 29 commercial banks from releasing, transferring, converting or otherwise dealing with funds belonging to the NGF within their custody. The judge further directed the banks to disclose, within 48 hours of service, whether the NGF maintains accounts containing the disputed funds. The banks are required to identify such accounts, their currencies, available balances and amounts preserved under the court’s order. The amount represents 100 million dollars, equivalent to the N135.55 billion, calculated at the exchange rate of N1,355.80 to the dollar. Justice Agbaza made the orders on Nov. 19, following the ex parte application and submissions by the claimant’s counsel, Emonye Adekwu, SAN, alongside Damilola Odesola, from Ade Okeaya-Inneh & Co. Law Firm. A certified true copy of the enrolled order by the court was obtained by the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Abuja. Iseghohi-Edwards, who carries on business as Edwards and Partners Law Firm, is seeking recovery of the money pursuant to an indemnity issued by the NGF. The claimant’s case is that the money belongs to him under an indemnity dated Dec. 20, 2018, issued by the NGF. The indemnity reportedly arose from an arrangement under which the Federal Government paid 100 million dollars to the NGF as a stakeholder. The money was to be held pending the determination of the Federal Government’s liability to Iseghohi-Edwards over legal and consultancy fees. The fees arose from services allegedly rendered in connection with the London and Paris Club loan transaction. Iseghohi-Edwards claimed he was retained by the Incorporated Trustees of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON) to represent the 774 local government councils in the London and Paris Clubs’ refund matters. He had instituted Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/856/2016 against the Federal Government over the outstanding professional fees. According to his court filings, the Federal High Court, on Feb. 16, 2018, delivered judgment establishing the government’s indebtedness of 318 million dollars. The claimant said the government subsequently made a part-payment of 159 million dollars through promissory notes. He contended that the judgment fulfilled the condition contained in the NGF’s indemnity, thereby making the 100 million dollars payable directly to him. item.title: Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia, bipolar disorder diagnosis
item.description: Former world heavyweight boxing champion, Tyson Fury, has disclosed that he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder in a forthcoming Netflix documentary about his life and career. According to Deadline , Fury made the revelation in the feature-length documentary titled Tyson Fury , which is scheduled for release later this month. The boxer said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia shortly after defeating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 to become the world heavyweight champion. He also disclosed that he received a bipolar disorder diagnosis in 2017. Reflecting on his mental health struggles in the documentary, Fury described experiencing periods of severe psychological distress. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100% thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much,” he reportedly said. Fury also recounted experiencing intense anxiety that frequently woke him in the middle of the night. He said he eventually sought professional help from a psychiatrist in London, who assessed him through a series of questions and identified depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder. The documentary also features contributions from his wife, Paris Fury, and father, John Fury, who discuss his mental health challenges. The post Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia, bipolar disorder diagnosis appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigerians Firmly Behind APC Despite Criticism And Insults — Yari
item.description: The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, has said the massive turnout at the party’s governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State demonstrates the people’s acceptance of the party despite what he described as campaigns of calumny and insults against it. Yari said the APC was consolidating its support base to secure victory at all levels in the 2027 general elections, attributing the party’s growing acceptance to its closeness to the masses. He stated this on Monday during the APC campaign flag-off held in Talata-Mafara, which attracted party faithful, support groups and members of the public. All Progressives Congress governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State on Monday, November 23, 2026. Crowds of party supporters welcomed Governor Dauda Lawal’s motorcade to Talata-Mafara town before proceeding to the town’s Eid ground, venue of the rally. Speaking at the event, Senator Yari said the large turnout reflected the enthusiasm and commitment of party members and supporters towards the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections. “Make sure this message gets to the public: we are determined to deliver victory for the APC, from President Tinubu down to members of the State House of Assembly. “The overwhelming response to our call demonstrates that, despite the insults and campaigns against the APC, the people of Zamfara have understood our message and are firmly behind the party,” he said. The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, and Governor Radda Dikko during the party’s governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State, on Monday, November 23, 2026. Also speaking, Governor Dauda Lawal expressed gratitude to party supporters for their show of solidarity, while commending the people for their resilience and commitment to peaceful coexistence. He reaffirmed his administration’s resolve to promote inclusive governance, equitable development and sustained engagement with communities across the state. “This crowd speaks for itself; there is very little to say other than to thank Almighty God. Whenever I turn around and see this mammoth crowd of supporters, I am filled with gratitude. “At this point, I will simply say, let us wait for election day and, ultimately, the swearing-in day,” Lawal said. The APC campaign train is expected to move to other local government areas of Zamfara State as the party intensifies its mobilisation and grassroots engagement ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Waste crisis: LAWMA launches nighttime evacuation gangs
item.description: …Plans over 10 regional offices ahead of Yuletide By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) has launched a nighttime waste evacuation operation across the state to tackle mounting refuse heaps and restore environmental sanitation ahead of the Christmas and New Year festivities. The exercise, which commenced on Monday night, began along the Isheri–Igando–LASU–Iba corridor, with sanitation teams and heavy-duty equipment deployed to clear identified waste black spots. LAWMA’s Acting Managing Director, Olajuwon Akinyemi, led the operation at Igando Bus Stop alongside the Acting Executive Director of Operations, Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director of Finance, Kunle Adebiyi. Speaking during the exercise, Akinyemi said the nighttime evacuation would be extended to other major entry routes and high-traffic corridors, including Ojota–Ikorodu Road, Mushin–Moshalashi axis and Lekki–Ajah corridor. He said the operation was aimed at restoring Lagos’s environmental appeal and providing a cleaner and healthier atmosphere for residents and visitors expected in the state during the busy December holiday season. To prevent cleared locations from becoming refuse dumps again, the agency said it was partnering with traditional institutions across the state to strengthen community monitoring and enforcement. Beyond the immediate clean-up exercise, Akinyemi announced plans to establish more than 10 regional offices across Lagos as part of efforts to decentralise the authority’s operations. He described the restructuring as non-negotiable, saying the regional offices would improve operational coordination, bring waste management services closer to communities, strengthen accountability and ensure faster responses to sanitation challenges. The LAWMA boss appealed to residents to remain patient with the state government as it works to address waste management challenges across the metropolis. He also urged residents to promptly report service failures by Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators through the authority’s official communication channels to enable it to enforce compliance. item.title: Omo Agege attack: ‘Enough is enough’, arrest, prosecute perpetrators – Keyamo tells police
item.description: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has condemned the killing of four persons in Ughelli, Delta State, following an outbreak of political violence, calling on security agencies to arrest and prosecute those responsible. Keyamo, in a statement issued on Monday, described the incident in his hometown as disturbing and said several other persons sustained injuries and were receiving treatment. He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished those injured a speedy recovery. The minister also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator allegedly by supporters of a political party in Asaba on November 7, 2026, urging law enforcement agencies to investigate both incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice. “I have been in touch with the top hierarchy of law enforcement agencies in the last one month over the rising wave of political violence and violent rhetoric in Delta State,” he said. Keyamo lamented that Delta, which had enjoyed relative political peace since 1999, was witnessing a disturbing rise in violence, insisting that political disagreements should not degenerate into killings. “Since 1999, Delta State has been a relatively peaceful state, politically. Our disagreements have never led to violence and killings. We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is ABSOLUTELY NO NEED for a descent into violence,” he said. He also criticised the slogan, “Rig and Die”, allegedly promoted by some political actors in Delta State and elsewhere, describing it as capable of escalating political tension and encouraging violence. The minister urged those promoting the slogan to reconsider their position, publicly withdraw it and apologise for overheating the political atmosphere. “Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country. As can be seen, anyone can be a victim,” he said. Keyamo maintained that only law enforcement agencies had the authority to deal with offenders, warning political leaders against encouraging their supporters to attack other citizens. He described such conduct as a sign of desperation and called on the Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address residents and warn those threatening violence. “I call on our leader and my elder brother, the Governor of Delta State and the Chief Security Officer of the State, Rt. Hon. Elder Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address Deltans and read the Riot Act against those who are threatening fire and brimstone. “Enough is enough,” he said. item.title: Fani-Kayode denies recall, meets Enikanolaiye
item.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has denied reports that he was recalled from his diplomatic posting, saying his visit to Abuja was to brief the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on his activities and consult with officials. Fani-Kayode spoke on Monday after meeting with the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja. He said the meeting was part of his official responsibilities and had nothing to do with reports circulating on social media that he had been recalled. “There have been reports on social media suggesting that I have been recalled. Those claims are simply untrue. “If I had been recalled, I doubt I would be standing here smiling after a cordial and productive meeting with the minister,” he said. The envoy explained that his visit was to submit official reports, consult with ministry officials, spend time with his family and prepare for their possible relocation to South Africa. He said he had initially planned to spend only a few days in South Africa following his posting but had extended his stay to complete necessary diplomatic procedures. Fani-Kayode also dismissed reports that his meeting with South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) over the controversy surrounding the omission of his speech during the presentation of his letters of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa amounted to a reprimand. He described the engagement as cordial and constructive, saying concerns were addressed professionally by both sides. “Our engagements with South African authorities have been cordial and constructive. Concerns have been raised on both sides in a professional diplomatic manner, and no reprimand of any kind occurred,” he said. The high commissioner reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening diplomatic relations between Nigeria and South Africa, particularly in trade, investment and other areas of mutual interest. “I believe strongly that if South Africa and Nigeria do not come together, it would affect the destiny of the whole African continent. We will do our best to build that bridge, and that bridge must never be broken,” he said. He, however, stressed that efforts to improve bilateral relations must not come at the expense of Nigeria’s national interests or the dignity, rights and welfare of Nigerians living in South Africa. Fani-Kayode expressed concern over persistent xenophobic attacks, killings and discriminatory rhetoric targeting Nigerians in the country. He also condemned attempts to portray Nigerians collectively as criminals and drug dealers, insisting that the actions of a few individuals should not be used to stigmatise an entire community. “As ambassador, I would be failing in my responsibility if I did not raise concerns about the treatment of Nigerians in South Africa. “Thousands of Nigerians in South Africa are law-abiding professionals, including doctors, lawyers, academics and entrepreneurs. A small minorit

item.title: It was an attempt on my life — Omo-Agege
item.description: Senator Omo-Agege, has alleged that the attack on his campaign train in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State was “premeditated”, saying it was part of an ongoing attempt to eliminate him. Speaking on Channels TV via Zoom, Omo-Agege said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others were critically injured when gunmen opened fire during his campaign event in Udu-Ere, Ughelli North. He said he was addressing supporters when the gunmen opened fire, adding that he heard them repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him. He said he survived the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services, DSS, security details. He said the attack occurred less than five minutes after he began his remarks at the campaign venue. His words: “This is premeditated. It is not something that just happened today. I just gave you the buildup. This thing has been going on. “As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of a vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started. The former Deputy Senate President said four members of his campaign organisation were killed in the attack, including former Federal Character Commissioner, and the immediate past president of the Urhobo Progress Union youth wing. The former senator said he heard the attackers shouting in English, “Omo-Agege, we want to kill,” while the shooting was ongoing. Omo-Agege called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation, saying he did not expect the Delta State Police Command to deliver justice. “We are appealing to the IGP to step in immediately and directly handle this investigation. We need justice,” he said. We need justice. We need justice for these four people who have been killed. We need justice for the 15 people who are critically injured and hospitalised right now,” he said. He also appealed to his supporters not to retaliate, saying the attack would not deter him from continuing his campaign. “If the idea is that this is supposed to deter me from going forward with the campaigns, it’s a very, very big mistake and a big lie. It ain’t going to happen,” Omo-Agege said. The post It was an attempt on my life — Omo-Agege appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Orgs that leak data 'prioritize corporate interests over customers' says Have I Been Pwned’s Troy Hunt
item.description: Troy Hunt, the founder of data breach reporting site Have I Been Pwned (HIBP), has revealed how organizations respond when he informs them they’ve leaked data – if they respond at all. Hunt gave Anthropic’s Claude access to an email inbox containing over eight years of his email correspondence and then asked the AI to write a post summarising them, a method he said “was the best way to highlight the behaviors I keep seeing across many breaches and subsequent disclosure efforts.” Writing in person, Hunt described those behaviors as “standoffish behavior, deliberate delays, heavy involvement from lawyers, and a constant theme: prioritizing corporate interests over those of their customers.” Once Claude takes over writing duties, it opens with the observation that Hunt sent his standard notification email to 73 organizations between March 2018 and November 2026 and also used website contact forms. Claude/Hunt focuses on the breach notifications that don’t go well, for example when first contact “often goes nowhere” because “many organisations have no obvious way to report a security incident.” Some organizations Hunt contacted logged his notifications as customer support requests. “In one case, Troy received three automated surveys asking him to rate the support he'd received,” Claude wrote, before observing “A message that an organization’s customer data is being traded among criminals ended up in the same queue as a question about a late delivery.” Once someone at victim organization gets the message, a common response is to say they can find no evidence of the breach. Others try to play down the incident, saying it was only a website defacement or that Hunt is re-reporting a previous breach the victim has already disclosed. If an organization accepts Hunt is probably onto something, it typically says it needs to investigate the matter. Claude’s take on Hunt’s mails suggests he responds by pointing out that this is an irresponsible approach, because while the investigation takes place, “people whose data has been taken don't know they need to change a password or watch for phishing.” Next, victims send in the lawyers who ask if their employer or client is legally required to reveal the breach. Hunt typically replies by saying it is up to the victim to decide if the incident meets the threshold that triggers mandatory disclosure requirements under local laws, but that he intends to notify HIBP users regardless. Victims don’t like hearing that and respond in three ways: Calling to discuss disclosure, rather than committing to it; Asking to see the wording HIBP will use in its disclosure, a request that sees Hunt refer the victim to the HIBP site for examples of the thousand-plus breach reports already on the site; Arguing that disclosure, not the breach, is the real harm. Hunt/Claude suggests that each argument victims use to avoid disclosure “sounds reasonable on its own,” but argues “Together, they mean the people most affected by the breach are t

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 24 – Galaxies Battle in the NGC 7771 Group
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 24 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Galaxies Battle in the NGC 7771 Group Explanation: After this galaxy battle, only one galaxy will remain. Already visible in the featured picture are rings and faint star swirls from previous gravitational encounters . Known collectively as the NGC 7771 Group , these galaxies lie almost 200 million light-years away toward the high-flying constellation Pegasus . The largest galaxy, barred spiral NGC 7771 on the lower right, is itself about 75,000 light-years across, and the galaxy on the upper left is spiral NGC 7769 , which is almost as large. As these and other smaller galaxies make repeated close passages, they will all likely merge into one very large galaxy. Playing out over billions of years, the merger process is understood to be a normal part of the evolution of galaxies . Studying galaxy clashes like this helps humanity to better understand the possible merger between our own Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies.
