item.title: Eruption Extends Iwo Jima’s Beach
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Eruption Extends Iwo Jima’s… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 26 November 11 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 26 November 11 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 26 November 11 Curtain Toggle 2-Up A volcanic eruption in the shallows near Iwo Jima has extended the Japanese island’s famed black sand beaches, at least temporarily. Signs of unrest began in late October 2026. On October 27, seismic sensors recorded a sharp uptick in activity, and Japan’s Meteorological Agency reported that the first photographs of the eruption were captured. Soon after, sensors on several satellites began to capture an array of observations. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured the left image on October 26, when the coast was still quiet. On November 11, Landsat 9 got its first clear view of the land the submarine volcano has built (right). A shortwave-infrared signature, a sign of the eruption’s heat, is shown in orange. A faint gray volcanic plume drifts southeast of the vent, and a streak of floating pumice stretches across the water in the same direction. A false-color backscatter radar image from the NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite offered an even earlier look at the eruption. On October 28, despite heavy cloud cover, the radar detected a large disturbance in the water in the same area that erupted in December 2023. When the clouds cleared in early November, the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors on NASA and NOAA satellites also captured signs of the ongoing eruption’s volcanic plumes and infrared signature . Japan’s Coast Guard released a report on November 16 confirming the formation of new land connected to the pre-existing beach. The eruption appears to have added roughly 50 hectares (125 acres) of new beach, about the area of 90 American football fields. That would enlarge the island by about 1.7 percent. The new land adjoins the southeast beach where American troops landed on February 19, 1945, beginning one of the bloodiest battles in the history of the U.S. Marines. The location of the eruption is no surprise to scientists. In addition to the 2023 eruption off the southeast coast, Iwo Jima had an eruption off its west coast in August 2025, said Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center. How long the new land will persist remains an open question. New land created by the 2023 eruption succumbed to wave action after

item.title: Cisco and OpenAI pitch eBPF kernel plugins as the way to tame the patchpocalypse
item.description: Cisco and OpenAI have released an open-source tool called Shirudo to implement compensating controls in Linux, potentially improving security for users who can’t quickly patch newly discovered software flaws. Shirudo relies on eBPF, the technology that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs in the Linux kernel. eBPF programs are effectively kernel plug-ins but don’t get unrestricted access to system resources. Developers have mostly used eBPF to create network functions that enable things like the open source Kubernetes observability and security tool Cilium , a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project. Cisco and OpenAI think eBPF can help organizations cope with the flood of 100,000-plus software flaws reported this year, many after the debut of AI-powered bug finders. The increased volume of flaws, and patches to fix them, is a problem for many organizations which already struggle to test fixes or find change windows in which to implement them. That problem has seen greater interest in “compensating controls” – changes to applications or infrastructure that harden them against flaws or malware, without requiring a patch. With Shirudo, Cisco and OpenAI are suggesting two things: The privileges eBPF programs enjoy make them a fine way to implement compensating controls for Linux; Agents should scan your infrastructure for vulnerabilities, then use tools like OpenAI’s Codex to write compensating controls as eBPF programs at machine speed. “Shirudo” is apparently the Japanese word for “shield,” so Cisco and OpenAI have called the eBPF programs the tool creates “shields.” The two companies envision humans checking every shield Shirudo creates before putting it into production. Shirudo is open source and available here . The two companies say they’ve already demonstrated it could mitigate the recently discovered flaws in Java without requiring downtime for an Elasticsearch implementation. Cisco and OpenAI are not alone in advocating for compensating controls. Third-party software maintenance outfits like Rimini Street have used them for years to protect software when their clients no longer have the right to access patches. VMware has introduced “virtual patching.” Palo Alto Networks and Rapid 7 also like this approach, and offer automation to develop controls. Where Cisco and OpenAI differ is their decision to make Shirudo open source , and their ambition that other players adapt and advance it. That offer is not entirely altruistic, as if Shirudo takes off it could create more demand for Codex. Cisco’s angle comes from the fact it owns Isovalent, an early champion of eBPF and the creator of both Cilium and the Tetragon sub-project on which Shirudo is based. Switchzilla is using eBPF in other products, so normalizing its use through an open source project can’t hurt. ®

item.title: Anthropic says Claude solved an age-old math problem, but the written proof is 250,000 pages of slop
item.description: The leaders of the great model houses, Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman, desperately want the world to believe AI is the skeleton key which will unlock the secrets of the universe. But if the AI can’t explain what it’s “proven,” are we actually any closer to understanding anything, or have we simply built another black box? That question is top of mind among mathematicians and computer scientists this week after Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge claimed to have solved a mathematical conjecture so elusive it's gone unproven for more than 150 years. The fact that this note came out one day after Anthropic's record-setting IPO is a coincidence, we're sure. In a four-page post to his website, the researcher described how with the help of Claude, he believes he has proven the Riemann Hypothesis, one of seven Millennium problems so complex and so important that the Clay Mathematics Institute has offered a $1 million prize to anyone who is successful in solving them. The Riemann Hypothesis, conjectured by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, contends that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function – those with a real part between zero and one – have a real part equal to 1/2. Confused? Don’t worry. We’ve linked to an explainer that goes into more detail here . What's important is that, if the Riemann Hypothesis is right, mathematicians can place tighter bounds on the difference between the actual distribution of prime numbers and mathematical estimates of that distribution. Researchers have previously attempted to disprove the conjecture through computational brute force, and therein have shown the hypothesis holds to at least 10 trillion zeros . There’s reason to believe that the Riemann Hypothesis is accurate, but the possibility remains that over a sufficiently long series the pattern might diverge. And so, more than 150 years after Riemann published his hypothesis, it has remained just that. Alpöge’s proof, if it can even be called that, is now the subject of great debate. The four pages in which Alpöge remarks on the discoveries he and Claude made aren’t exactly a proof, but rather 14 tarballs worth of Lean code totaling roughly 240 MB. Lean is an open source programming language commonly used to help validate mathematical proofs. The Clay Mathematics Institute, which oversees the seven Millennium Problems, has promoted the Riemann Hypothesis from “unsolved” to “active” status, but it is not yet considered solved. For Clay to consider the problem solved and award the prize, the proposed solution must be published in a qualifying outlet, remain available for scrutiny for at least two years, and receive broad acceptance from the mathematics community. As it stands, Alpöge describes the 250,000 pages of text generated by the model for its written proof as a “massive unreadable travesty of ‘slop.’” Not long after Alpöge's remarks and Lean code were published, Stanford mathematician Ravi Vakil released a nearly 1,000-pag

On Monday, Ladybird developer Andreas Kling announced that the browser is launching in alpha on macOS and Linux following more than four years of development. The release makes Ladybird the first browser in years to arrive with an entirely new engine. We've seen many engines emerge over time, but the most popular browsers use just three today: Gecko, Blink, and WebKit. item.title: Danielle Adewusi Honours Benin Kingdom Royalty in a Self-Designed National Costume at Miss Universe 2026
item.description: Danielle Adewusi displays the sweeping circular halo backpiece and floor-length beaded train of her Benin-inspired national costume. A little Benin royalty on the Miss Universe stage? Danielle Adewusi is bringing it to Puerto Rico. For the 75th edition of the competition in San Juan, Miss Universe Nigeria 2026 has arrived at the National Costume runway with Daughter of the Coral Throne, an Edo-inspired creation that brings the history of the ancient Benin Kingdom into the spotlight. And in case you missed that detail, Danielle designed the entire look herself. Now, where do we begin with this costume? The red coral beads are everywhere, from the sheer-panelled corset bodysuit and its sweetheart neckline, trimmed with gold-toned cowrie shells, to the floor-sweeping beaded overskirt and train. Look a little closer and there’s a miniature Queen Idia mask emblem at the hip. Danielle Adewusi holds her gold ceremonial staff diagonally across Daughter of the Coral Throne against a waterside garden backdrop. Then comes the fan-shaped coral bead headpiece, followed by a sweeping circular halo backpiece with cascading bead fringes. A tall gold ceremonial staff, topped with a sculpted Queen Idia mask, completes the look. Sculpted bronze-gold motifs and thousands of beads bring the whole tribute together, with each detail drawing from the artistry and royal traditions of the Benin Kingdom. Danielle Adewusi pairs warm bronzed makeup and sleek cornrows with red coral beadwork and gold cowrie detailing. Of course, Danielle isn’t leaving us to admire the costume without knowing what inspired it. She shared the story behind Daughter of the Coral Throne, explaining how she wanted to honour her Edo heritage and celebrate a kingdom whose history and identity remain, even after many of its treasures were taken: For my Miss Universe National Costume, I honour my Edo heritage and the extraordinary legacy of the ancient Kingdom of Benin, one of Africa’s greatest civilisations… Daughter of the Coral Throne reimagines the splendour of Edo royalty through contemporary African couture. Thousands of coral-inspired beads celebrate the prestige and authority of Benin royalty, while gold detailing pays tribute to the kingdom’s master craftsmen. The circular backpiece symbolises the continuity of our ancestry, radiating across generations. In my hand, a golden ceremonial staff honours the Oba of Benin, representing leadership, royal authority and an unbroken lineage. And as I follow in my mother’s footsteps, 35 years after she wore the Miss Universe Nigeria crown, I am reminded that legacy is not simply inherited. It is preserved, honoured and carried forward. Danielle Adewusi honours her Edo heritage in Daughter of the Coral Throne ahead of the Miss Universe 2026 finale There’s a personal connection to this Miss Universe journey, too. item.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
item.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal. "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer, associate professor at OSU's Department of Botany and Plant Pathology, said in a statement . "That's an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the moon." To grow the spuds, the scientists used five different materials that are similar to regolith , the dust and rocks that cover the moon's surface. The moon contains various regions with unique surface makeups, so the materials they used simulated regolith from both lunar mare and lunar highland regions. The secret ingredient was vermicompost, a soil that's rich in nutrients. The team added different levels of vermicompost to the simulated regolith to grow the potatoes. They figured out that fake regolith mixed with 30 percent vermicompost worked about as well as growing potatoes with regular soil. Oregon State University researchers David Handy and Aymeric Goyer studying potatoes grown in lunar regolith. (Image credit: Aymeric Goyer/David Handy/OSU) "We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith by reducing plant exposure to harmful compounds," David Handy, a postdoctoral researcher in Goyer's lab, said in the same statement. The idea is that astronauts in the future could bring a little nutrient-rich soil with them and mix it with regolith to grow potatoes. After all, it'd cost a ton to ship all that food from Earth. NASA funding supported this research.

item.title: Trump halts Iowa detonation, says new governor to blame if it blows accidentally
item.description: President Trump took to social media Monday afternoon to announce that he has ordered the US military to halt plans to detonate 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa. Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa's governor-elect, who won't be sworn into office until January. The Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP). Iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand. The environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, claimed in an emergency court filing that the Army had not fully considered safer options for disposing of the lead azide before planning the detonation. item.title: Inception - possibly a ShinyHunters reboot - claims seven victims in a week
item.description: Don't mind the recent arrests. The ShinyHunters extortion gang may still be operating, just under the new name of Inception, according to Okta's threat intelligence group. ShinyHunters is the brash cybercriminal group that, most recently, breached rival gang Clop before hacking the FBI , resulting in at least three arrests of key suspects in September and October. The crims - and their old data leak site - have since gone dark. “While this threat cluster has changed their brand affiliation, the operators remain active in targeting organizations with voice phishing attacks and account takeovers resulting in data theft and extortion,” Okta threat hunters Moussa Diallo and Katie Nickels said on Monday. Okta tracks this threat cluster as O-UNC-053 - the “O-UNC” prefix stands for an Okta Uncategorized cluster, and it uses this label before formally attributing the activity to a named threat group. While Okta hasn't formally confirmed O-UNC-053 to be the same crime crew as ShinyHunters, the identity and access management provider’s researchers note that it does use nearly identical social engineering tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA). Plus, they note: O-UNC-053 operators change the themes of their phishing domains about every four to six weeks, and they also post claimed victims on ShinyHunters’ data leak site. In November, however, organizations targeted by O-UNC-053 began appearing on a new data leak site branded as Inception and not ShinyHunters. The first five - Advanced Micro Devices, Cigna Healthcare, Paychex, PepsiCo, and Henry Schein - appeared November 17 on the site, and all were marked “leaked.” Soon after, security maven Dominic Alvieri questioned if Inception was linked to ShinyHunters. “ShinyHunters are not all in jail,” he wrote on social media. On November 19, AutoZone appeared on the site, with Inception again claiming to have leaked the auto-parts retailer's files. On Saturday, EV technology firm Lucid Group joined the claimed victims. None of the seven companies have confirmed breaches, and none responded to The Register ’s inquiries. We will update this story when we receive more information. Okta Threat Intelligence “is unable to validate if published data is authentic,” the researchers said in response to our questions. In the Monday report, the Okta team does note that Inception’s new data leak site listings “included multiple targets for which Okta Threat Intelligence previously observed O-UNC-053 infrastructure registration.” The infrastructure was registered between six and 19 days before Inception listed the companies on its leak site, and this gap “is consistent with prior shifts from Com-affiliated actors,” Diallo and Nickels added. item.title: The Apple Watch Series 12 is cheaper than ever ahead of Black Friday
item.description: The Apple Watch Series 12 is on sale in multiple configurations. | Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge If you’re still sporting an Apple Watch that launched five or so years ago, now is a good time to upgrade. Apple’s latest smartwatch, the 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 with Wi-Fi and GPS connectivity, has dropped to a new all-time low of $299 ($100 off) at Amazon and Walmart , beating its most sale price by $30. If you prefer a larger size, the 46mm model is on sale for $349 ($100 off) at Amazon and Walmart , beating its previous low by $30. Apple Watch Series 12 Where to Buy: $399 $299 at Amazon (GPS, 42mm) $399 $299 at Walmart (GPS, 42mm) $449 $349 at Amazon (GPS, 46mm) The Series 12 stands out compared to previous models with its new AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, which are made possible by Apple’s new S11 chip. For example, the watch can alert you when it detects sounds like a doorbell, alarm, or even a baby’s cry, while other upcoming features like Live Rewind and Siri Recap lets you look back at a transcript of the previous 15 seconds of conversation and get a high-level overview of the conversations you had that day. The new chip also makes Siri more responsive, so you can get answers to questions with less waiting around. It’s not all about AI, though. The Series 12 also features redesigned health sensors that can now track your heart rate every five seconds even when you’re not exercising, which is particularly help if you have a chronic condition and need to keep a closer eye on your heart rate. It also introduces a new readiness score to help you decide how prepared your body is for the day. Other highlights include easier navigation with simple pinch gestures, and faster charging, which helps to make up for the fact that battery life is rated at up to 24 hours on a single charge, just like the previous-generation model. In our testing, the watch went from 20 to 64 percent charge in just 20 minutes, making it relatively easy to top up while showering or getting ready for the day. item.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
item.description: On Monday, Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX, alleging that Grok continues to sexualize, unchecked, real photos of mostly women and children. SpaceX acquired xAI in February and now must handle the ongoing reckoning over the controversial rollout of Grok’s “spicy mode”—a model feature Musk hyped but was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and child sex abuse images (CSAM). Initial safeguards were so lax that Grok sometimes generated nude images without being asked . Although X Safety and xAI (now known as SpaceXSI) were silent at first , Musk’s companies eventually apologized and claimed that additional safeguards were implemented and policies redesigned to block harmful outputs. However, state attorneys general alleged that those statements were “misleading” and that SpaceXSI instead quietly “embraced” sexualized content to seize more AI market share, as Grok continues to generate NCII and CSAM today. Read full article Comments

item.description:
Tariq is the Editor-in-Chief of Space.com based out of our New York City office and joined the team in 2001, first as an intern and staff writer, and later as an editor. He covers human spaceflight, exploration and space science, as well as skywatching and entertainment. He became Space.com's Managing Editor in 2009 and Editor-in-Chief in 2019. In October 2022, Tariq received the Harry Kolcum Award for excellence in space reporting from the National Space Club Florida Committee. In June 2025, the National Space Society awarded him the Space Pioneer Award for Excellence in Mass Media at the International Space Development Conference in Orlando, Florida.

Hailing from Stockton, California (where he attended the same high school as NASA astronaut Jose Hernandez), Tariq studied print journalism and astronomy at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, earning a bachelor's degree in journalism in 1999 along with a minor in astronomy. He then served as a staff reporter for The Los Angeles Times covering education and city beats in La Habra and Fullerton in Orange County for the Our Times sections.

In 2000, Tariq became the city reporter for the Huntington Beach Independent, a weekly publication of the Los Angeles Times, covering local politics and events, crime, business and environmental issues. He left the Los Angeles Times in 2001 to study science journalism at New York University, where he earned a master's degree in 2002 from NYU's Science and Environmental Reporting Program (now the Science, Health and Environmental Reporting Program) under the direction of space reporter William Burrows.

Tariq first joined Space.com as an intern in September 2001 while also serving as a research assistant for nutrition writer Gary Taubes and writing freelance projects, where his work appeared in The Scientist and Laboratory Equipment Magazine. He became a full-time reporter covering spaceflight in 2004, with this first launch being NASA's STS-114 Return to Flight mission in July 2005.

Tariq is also an Eagle Scout (yes, he has the Space Exploration merit badge) and went to Space Camp four times as a kid and a fifth time as an adult. When not writing about space, you can find Tariq watching the latest Star Trek TV series, sci-fi movies and reading about hippos, his favorite animal. You can find Tariq at Space.com and as the co-host to the This Week In Space podcast with space historian Rod Pyle on the TWiT network. To see his latest project, you can follow Tariq on Twitter @tariqjmalik.

item.title: Amazon scoops up AI accelerator tech to keep chips busy at all times
item.description: Amazon has agreed to buy AI optimization technology from an Israeli startup in a bid to speed up its inference operations. The house of Bezos on Monday announced a deal to purchase proprietary AI acceleration tech from Decart AI, known as the Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), for an undisclosed amount. Amazon also plans to bring Decart’s three founders and their engineering team into the fold. Decart’s DOS is designed to push AI hardware closer to its maximum performance across different AI models and hardware platforms. The company claims that most AI chips live their lives without reaching their full potential – practically a sin in this age of increased hardware costs and limited availability – and DOS aims to fix that by operating between the model and the chip, optimizing kernels, compilers, and runtimes for the underlying hardware “so every core stays busy.” DOS is hardware-agnostic, with Decart saying it supports Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, and, most critically for our purposes here, AWS Trainium chips. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost,” Peter DeSantis, Amazon SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, and quantum computing, said in the announcement. “That's the pillar Trainium and our AI efforts are built on, and from our earliest work with Decart, we knew they … would help us push it even further.” Decart doesn’t offer much in the way of details about its proprietary AI-maxxing tech, but claims it can reduce latency, improve throughput, and reduce the costs associated with training and inference runs. An Amazon spokesperson clarified to The Register that the deal is an asset purchase and not a full company acquisition, with Amazon only acquiring DOS and the tech behind it as well as personnel. As for what may become of Decart after the deal, that’s unclear. Amazon told us to reach out to Decart to learn what may happen to any remaining employees and the company’s other technology, but we didn’t hear back. Along with offering its optimization stack, Decart has a couple of different AI models: Lucy, a live video model marketed toward advertisers, live streamers, and the like; and Oasis, a world model AI marketed toward companies working on embodied AI applications. Decart’s non-DOS assets weren’t mentioned in the press release, and per the Amazon spokesperson we talked to, that means they weren’t part of the deal. We can’t imagine that the Decart team is too upset about the potential abandonment of those models, though: While neither company has disclosed a price, Bloomberg claims its sources value the deal at around $7.5 billion. If Bloomberg's figure is accurate, that would make this deal one of the most expensive in Amazon’s history, right between its $3.9 billion acquisition of One Medical and its $8.5 billion purchase of film studio MGM . ®

item.title: NASA Awards Contract for NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network Program
item.description: Credit: NASA NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments on NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) satellites. The cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, and time-and-materials hybrid contract has a value of $290.6 million. The period of performance runs from Nov. 23 through April 1, 2042. The work will take place at the awardee’s facility. Under the contract, Northrop Grumman will provide the design, development, production, testing, and mission support for three SMBA instruments, the next generation of low Earth orbit microwave sounders. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, is managing the acquisition, and NOAA will own and operate the instruments and deliver the data to users worldwide. Microwave sounders provide critical measurements of temperature and moisture in the atmosphere, which significantly influence weather patterns. The SMBA instruments could improve the medium-range forecasts for NOAA’s National Weather Service. The NEON mission is a collaboration between NASA and NOAA. The mission is led by NOAA, which provides funding, technical requirements, and postlaunch operations. NASA will manage the development of the NEON satellites and launch them for NOAA. NASA and NOAA will work with commercial partners to design and build the NEON spacecraft and instruments. Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close. Strive pauses after two small buys The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that. Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion. The filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again. Most of the stack was built quickly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run. Cash and preferred holdings Strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. The filing does not break out what drove the change. The company also still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred stock. The fair value of that position fell to $47.3 million from $50.5 million, a drop of about $3.2 million, with the share count unchanged. Share counts were also flat. Strive reported 118,133,002 Class A shares and 9,198,107 Class B shares, for 127,331,109 effective common shares. Outstanding preferred stood at 14,030,176 shares of SATA and 7,141,037 shares of SATS, the 15% perpetual preferred it has used to fund most of its purchases. Strive’s holdings rose from 43,153 bitcoin on Nov. 6 to 43,404 on Nov. 13, and the filing shows no change since. With no common or preferred stock sold, the company raised no new capital through its offering programs last week, which left cash as its main resource for dividends and operations. Shares rally, then fade with the market Strive shares were trading near $15.55 at 3:56 p.m. ET on Monday, up about 7.1% from Friday’s close of $14.51, according to Yahoo Finance. The stock opened near $17.64, a gain of more than 20%, and gave back much of it through the session. item.title: Baby News and Beautiful Blue! Mitchel Ukachukwu Is Expecting Her First Child
item.description: Mitchel Ukachukwu celebrates her pregnancy announcement in a strapless pleated royal blue gown and neck scarf. Baby news and a beautiful maternity reveal? Congratulations are certainly in order for Mitchel Ukachukwu (née Ihezue )! The former Most Beautiful Girl in Nigeria (MBGN) and Miss Universe Nigeria titleholder is expecting her first child, and she’s sharing the lovely news with photographs that have us smiling and admiring her royal blue maternity look. If this is how Mitchel is introducing us to her maternity style, we’re already looking forward to more. For her pregnancy announcement, Mitchel slipped into a strapless, floor-length royal blue gown crafted from finely pleated, semi-sheer organza. The sweetheart neckline is gathered into a knot just above her baby bump, while the skirt falls into soft pleats, opening into a high front slit. She added a matching pleated neck scarf that flows into a long cape, with sweeping lengths of royal blue fabric suspended around her to complete the setting. Mitchel Ukachukwu marks her pregnancy reveal in a pleated royal blue gown with sweeping fabric waves. We also love how the beauty details bring everything together: chestnut-brown hair in glossy, side-parted Hollywood waves, soft bronzed makeup and understated gold jewellery. And, of course, those sweet photographs of her cradling her bump make the announcement all the more lovely. Many of us first got to know Mitchel as Mitchel Ihezue when she won the Most Beautiful Girl in Nigeria crown in 2017, before going on to claim the Miss Universe Nigeria title in 2023. Her pregnancy announcement comes nearly three years after she married Nigerian billionaire businessman and Prince Nicholas Ukachukwu , popularly known as Ikukuoma. The couple celebrated their union in December 2023 with traditional and white wedding ceremonies in Anambra State and are now preparing to welcome their first child. Mitchel Ukachukwu cradles her baby bump while wearing a knotted sweetheart royal blue gown and gold accessories. Sharing the news, Mitchel wrote, “Soooo….we cooked! The bestowment of God’s goodness. God is Faithful.” And they really did cook! With their first child on the way, Mitchel and Nicholas are getting ready for a new chapter together. We can’t be the only ones already looking forward to seeing how Mitchel styles her baby bump, can we? Mitchel Ukachukwu showcases the sheer pleated skirt and flowing cape of her royal blue maternity outfit. *** Photo Credit: Mitchel Ukachukwu/Instagram The post Baby News and Beautiful Blue! item.title: Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return The bitcoin price slipped back to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon, giving up nearly all of its morning spike even as Wall Street held one of its biggest rallies in years on Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Bitcoin jumped above $64,000 shortly after the Nvidia news broke before 10 a.m. ET and topped out near $64,500. The move reversed within hours , and the bitcoin price dipped to around $60,800 by 2:45 p.m. ET. It remains up only modestly on the day. The round trip was costly for leveraged traders. Bitcoin liquidations reached about $321 million , with short bets making up $224 million of that total. Liquidations across the broader crypto market topped $762 million. Stocks hold gains as bitcoin fades Stocks kept climbing while bitcoin slid. The Nasdaq Composite was up about 6.9% near 24,170 at about 3:40 p.m. ET, while the S&P 500 gained about 5% and the Dow rose about 3.2%. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days before Monday. Nvidia (NVDA) led the move, trading near $165.66, up about 32% from Friday’s close of $125.53. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, 12 days after he resigned. A stronger dollar may be weighing on the bitcoin price. The dollar index rose about 0.65% to 104.40 , its strongest level since April 2025, as the stock rebound put more Federal Reserve rate hikes back in play. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point hike remains the base case. Adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, pointed to steady selling during U.S. market hours since Huang first stepped down. “Bitcoin has fallen in seven of the eight U.S. sessions since Huang went, today’s included, and last week each session’s fall lined up with that day’s ETF outflow,” he said. Crypto stocks keep most of their gains Crypto stocks held up far better than the bitcoin price. Strategy (MSTR) was up about 9.3% near $85.03 in afternoon trading, after it disclosed a purchase of 457 bitcoin last week. Coinbase (COIN) gained about 6.7% to near $108.78, Robinhood (HOOD) rose about 8.8% to near $67.64 and Circle (CRCL) added about 8% to near $51.33. Miners with AI data center businesses posted the biggest moves. IREN (IREN) jumped about 23% to near $14.57, CleanSpark (CLSK) rose about 12.6% and MARA Holdings (MARA) gained about 10%. Core Scientific (CORZ) climbed about 9.4% and Riot Platforms (RIOT) added about 7.1%. ETF flows and inflation data are next Monday’s spot bitcoin ETF flows are the next test. The funds lost about $1.79 billion last week, their fourth straight week of net outflows, as bitcoin slid toward $58,000 on Friday and hit a weekend low near $55,100. “Tonight’s ETF flow figure is the first real test of this bounce,” Haeems said. item.title: Surveillance pricing uses our personal data to make us pay more
item.description: “It costs what it costs” is a mindset I’ve found useful when encountering a sizable, but highly necessary or desired, expense. The sentiment encourages me to accept the price because that’s the accepted value of the gadget, app, or service that I really need or want. But with surveillance pricing, that comfort is no longer a given. I could end up paying more for my TV because of where I am or more for a software subscription because of my age. Surveillance pricing leverages data collected from our web history , smart devices , and apps with the goal of getting us to pay more. That obfuscates the value of products, challenges smart shopping and budgets, and makes it harder for people to get products and services at a fair price. Read full article Comments

item.title: Bluetooth brakes are broken as researchers find anyone can control them
item.description: Imagine something as mission-critical as the brakes on a trailer being vulnerable to unauthorized control. One Australian manufacturer made the interesting choice of building Bluetooth into a trailer brake controller without adequately securing its critical braking functions. Anyone within Bluetooth range of an unpatched Elecbrakes trailer controller could potentially trigger its brakes or apply more braking force than intended, without needing to authenticate. The discovery comes courtesy of a pair of security researchers from Element Digital, Patrick Forck and Jeremy McCarthy. Their investigation began earlier this year when Forck was driving down the road and noticed that his physical Elecbrakes In-Car Remote had connected to someone else's trailer without pairing or prompting him. “It had connected mid-drive, without pairing or a prompt, to a brake controller that wasn’t mine, on a trailer I’d never seen, belonging to a driver who had no idea,” the researchers wrote . That one-off connection triggered a full-scale investigation by the pair. For those unfamiliar with trailer brake controllers, these devices are commonly used on larger trailers. Australian manufacturer Elecbrakes sells such controllers in Australia and New Zealand. Depending on jurisdiction, trailers over a certain weight are required to have their own braking system, which Elecbrakes manufactures. Elecbrakes offers two versions that are designed to be easier to install than traditional controllers: One that’s mounted in a vehicle, and one that is mounted directly on a trailer. That trailer-mounted unit can receive Bluetooth commands from the Elecbrakes smartphone app or a separate in-car remote. Given the importance of such control units to road safety, it’s easy to imagine how serious such a vulnerability could be if it proved to be easy to exploit, and boy, did it. Forck and McCarthy admitted they’re infrastructure security guys, not software devs, so they turned to Claude Code to dissect a decompiled copy of the Elecbrakes app, which Claude was happy to oblige. “What came back from the analysis was a map of the device’s entire Bluetooth GATT profile: 47 characteristics across four services, commands sent as plain unencrypted byte arrays, no checksums, no sequence numbers,” the researchers noted. To make matters worse, there was no authentication required for critical braking commands, even though other Bluetooth functions required pairing. Claude then built a web app that ran in Chrome which was able to access the Bluetooth controls for a nearby Elecbrakes system, and they were able to modify practically every aspect of brake control on a unit owned by one of them. Pairing failed on a few attempts, but not where it mattered: It allowed the connection without issue for actual brake control. item.title: Reports: Russia may launch nuclear weapon into orbit as soon as next month
item.description: Western intelligence officials worry that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit before the end of the year, suggesting the country's development of a satellite-killing weapon of mass destruction is more advanced than previously thought, German media reported Monday. The orbiting nuclear weapon would threaten thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, including military and commercial communications networks like Starshield and Starlink. A nuclear-armed satellite would also put at risk Western military surveillance satellites and human spaceflight platforms like the International Space Station. A nuclear detonation in orbit would be indiscriminate, also knocking out Russia's own spacecraft and Chinese satellites. US lawmakers briefed on government intelligence first disclosed Russia's ambition to deploy a space-based nuclear weapon in early 2024 . At the time, US officials said Russia had launched a test satellite in 2022 to test the effects of radiation on space hardware and pave the way for a future nuclear-armed craft, but that Russia had not yet sent a nuclear weapon into orbit. item.title: How sci‑fi imagines sports in microgravity, and how zero‑g sports might actually work
item.description:
Alan Bradley is an experienced tech and culture writer with more than 20 years covering gaming, tech, and hardware. He has served as commerce director and in senior editorial roles at major publications. His work has appeared in Rolling Stone, U.S. News & World Report, PCMag, TechRadar, GamesRadar+, CNET, Live Science, Variety, and many other outlets. Alan is also a novelist—his debut novel, the urban fantasy The Sixth Borough, is available now.

Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game. There was even Space Jam 's alien basketball game for the fate of the planet, though the gravity-defying antics there come from cartoon shenanigans rather than a zero-g playing field. As humanity edges closer to colonizing our neighbors through projects like the Artemis Program and its ambition to establish habitats on the moon, our imaginations have to expand to encompass not only how we'll live in space but also how we'll play. The rules change when gravity disappears (Image credit: Zero-G) We rarely think about it in an Earth context, but every sport is heavily influenced by gravity. It defines how balls arc, how quickly players can move, and even how we orient ourselves in play spaces. Remove the gravity, and all of those assumptions and mechanics evaporate as well. "First of all, in zero g, Isaac Newton will win every time," Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, told Space. Les is a physicist with over 35 years of experience working at Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, as well as a science fiction author. "'For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction,'" quotes Johnson. "This is very difficult to simulate in real life due to gravity; special effects often try to compensate. With today’s AI and green screens, it can actually look good on screen." In a microgravity scenario, the concept of up and down is no longer relevant. Suddenly, the playing field expands from a single, fixed plane to a fully three-dimensional space that includes height. (Image credit: Netflix) Momentum is also a completely different beast. Instead of being able to quickly stop and pivot the way you can during terrestrial sports, once you start moving in microgravity, you keep going until something stops you. It takes the trickiness of moving on ice in sports like hockey and increases it by several orders of magnitude. Of course, the havoc wouldn't stop with m

item.title: How to Style Green Lace for Asoebi Like Mercy Aigbe
item.description: Structural tailoring meets monochrome colour play in Mercy Aigbe’s olive and sage green asoebi look. Whenever a green dress code lands in your inbox for an upcoming wedding or celebration, the goal is always making the colour feel fresh and flattering rather than predictable. Nollywood star and filmmaker, Mercy Aigbe just gave us the sweetest blueprint for how to wear green lace for asoebi without letting heavy fabric wear you . The secret to nailing monochrome green for asoebi is mixing your shades and textures so you avoid one flat block of colour from head to toe. Mercy’s gown pairs a smooth, velvety olive corset—complete with visible boning and a central trail of beaded leaf appliqués—with a heavily beaded mermaid skirt in the same olive family . Mercy Aigbe showcases the full silhouette of her olive green corset and beaded lace mermaid gown paired with a marbled sage headtie. Keeping the bodice matte while the skirt sparkles lets the silhouette breathe, and crowning the outfit with a lighter, marbled sage headtie (gele) brightens up the face far better than a dark green wrap ever could. When taking your own green lace to the tailor, borrow her structural tricks: an asymmetrical off-the-shoulder neckline with 3D floral cutouts draws the eye upward, while a diagonal beaded sash-peplum along one hip creates curves without adding bulk around your waist. Mercy Aigbe pairs her olive green lace outfit with a deep red crystal crescent clutch and matching red manicure. As for how to accessorise a green monochrome outfit, skip the usual all-gold default and bring in a rich contrast colour. Olive and sage sit right opposite red on the colour wheel, which is why Mercy’s gold jewellery set with dark red stones, crescent red crystal clutch, and glossy red nails pop so well against the green . Paired with warm golden-bronze eyeshadow and a glossy nude-brown lip , the whole look feels balanced, celebratory, and ready for any guest list. item.title: Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined Last Week, Holds None
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined Last Week, Holds None Bitdeer sold every bitcoin it mined last week and still holds none of its own, the company said in its latest weekly update, continuing a nearly year-long strategy of turning production into cash after a weekend plunge in the bitcoin price. The Singapore-based miner reported output of 281.1 BTC and sales of 281.1 BTC for the week, for a net addition of zero. Its pure holdings, which exclude customer deposits, were zero as of Nov. 20. The sales came as bitcoin fell to a weekend low of $55,106 early Saturday at 1:17 AM ET, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The price has since bounced to near $62,700 as of 11:23 AM ET Monday. Bitdeer’s reserve has been drained all year Bitdeer’s treasury shrank from roughly 2,000 BTC at the end of 2025 to zero by Feb. 20, when Bitcoin Magazine reported the miner had liquidated its reserve over eight weeks. At the time, the company said the move should not be a concern for the broader market. Bitdeer’s filings show how little it has kept since. In its third-quarter results, filed with the SEC on a Form 6-K on Nov. 10, the company listed 47 BTC held at Sept. 30, down from 2,029 a year earlier. Its September production update showed 61 BTC held at the end of August. The company mined 1,355 BTC in September and 3,855 BTC in the third quarter, compared with 1,109 BTC in the same quarter of 2025. Self-mining margins stay thin Bitdeer has grown its fleet quickly. Self-mining hashrate reached 82.3 exahashes per second in the third quarter, up from 35.0 a year earlier, with another 28.7 exahashes per second of co-mining at third-party sites, the quarterly report shows . The economics are tight. Self-mining generated $217.5 million in revenue in the quarter but only $6.2 million in gross profit. Electricity averaged $47 per megawatt-hour, and the fleet ran at 15.4 joules per terahash. Bitdeer posted record revenue of $320.7 million and adjusted EBITDA of $69.6 million, but a net loss of $125.5 million. That included a $54.6 million non-cash loss tied to a bitcoin-collateralized loan from a related party. Bitdeer also reported $213.7 million in cash and restricted cash, and its board authorized a new $100 million share repurchase program on Oct. 8. Borrowing against coins instead of selling them Not every miner is selling. American Bitcoin secured a $150 million revolving credit line from FalconX on Monday that is backed by its bitcoin. The company said the facility lets it raise cash without drawing down its reserve. The loan carries a 5.95% fee and an initial collateral ratio of 143%. Fully drawing it would require about $214.5 million in pledged bitcoin. American Bitcoin has not said whether it has drawn on the line, and its release lists the risk that pledged coins could be liquidated if prices fall. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
item.description: null On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit. The company's triple-core Falcon Heavy boosters can also land vertically and its massive Starship megarocket can even return to the launch site to be caught by giant metal arms. But in the end, Blue Origin did it first. Blue Origin's New Shepard booster landing kicked off an era of vertical launch and vertical landings for rockets that continues to this day. It may have even outlasted the New Shepard rocket. Since that first landing, Blue Origin has launched 17 suborbital astronaut flights with New Shepard, and 21 more uncrewed flights for a total of 38 missions between April 2015 and 2026. The company reused its New Shepard boosters repeatedly (though it did lose one during an uncrewed launch after a technical issue.) But in January 2026, the company announced a pause in New Shepard flights for two years so that it could focus on moon lander projects. But Blue Origin did not abandon rocket landings. Indeed, the company's success with New Shepard led it to build vertical landing into its larger orbital rocket, New Glenn, which made its first successful landing 2025 — nearly 10 years after that first touchdown. Blue Origin has since reflown a New Glenn booster , and is developing a new rocket engine called Northstar for even better performance. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Critical Cisco remote code execution bug under attack
item.description: Attackers are currently exploiting a critical vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway that allows them to remotely execute commands as root without any authentication, according to warnings from the US government and security researchers. CVE-2026-76466 , which carries a 9.8 CVSS rating, affects Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E gateways configured in clusters, both virtual and physical appliances running vulnerable software. These provide firewall traversal, VPN-less remote access, and call routing for remote users connecting to voice, video, and messaging collaboration services. The bug involves hard-coded authentication credentials and insufficient certificate validation in clustered Expressway deployments. “An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands,” Cisco said in October, when it disclosed the bug and issued a software update that fixed the flaw. “A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device.” At the time, the networking vendor said it wasn’t aware of any abuse of the vulnerability. That all changed late last week, however, when Russian security firm F6 said it was investigating “the first observed case” of miscreants exploiting CVE-2026-76466, shortly after a public proof-of-concept exploit became available. “The attackers initially compromised two Cisco Expressway internet-facing devices,” F6’s Cyber Defense Center said on Thursday. “Through one of them, they gained access to two additional cluster nodes located on the organization’s internal network. After obtaining root access, the attackers began preparing tooling for further lateral movement across the infrastructure.” Specifically, the criminals prepared custom Python code to scan the victim’s network and identify files and folders shared over the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. The scripts were also designed to interact with SQL Server and WinRM, and search GitLab repositories for credentials and other sensitive information. The Python scripts used in the attack indicated that the operator used an AI assistant, according to F6. The security shop also noted that one of the key indicators of compromise is a nodeup “wombat@127.0.0.1” entry in the Erlang system log (erlang.log) on affected Cisco Expressway devices. A day later, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-76466 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and told federal agencies to patch by Monday. Cisco updated its advisory on Monday to acknowledge CISA’s addition, while noting that it has no direct evidence of active exploitation. The Register reached out to the networking and security vendor for additional details about the scope of the attacks, but did not receive any response. We will update this story as we learn more. ®

item.title: Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s A solo miner running about 11 terahashes per second has mined Bitcoin block 977,057, collecting a reward of 3.1287 BTC, or about $191,000, on a machine that makes up roughly one-millionth of a percent of the network. The block was found through the solo service at CKpool on Sunday, Nov. 22, at about 7:54 a.m. ET. The reward is the 3.125 BTC subsidy plus about 0.0037 BTC in transaction fees, and it was worth roughly $191,000 at bitcoin’s price when the block landed. How the solo block played out The block holds 584 transactions. Its coinbase transaction pays 3.0661 BTC to a single address and 0.0626 BTC, about 2% of the reward, to a second output. That split matches the service’s 2% fee, which means the miner’s take is a little over $186,000. Con Kolivas, the developer behind CKpool, congratulated the miner on X, whose address he abbreviated as bc1q~zy9j. It matches the end of the address that received the payout. Kolivas called it the 323rd block found on the service and “yet another lucky one.” He said the miner had only about 11.1 TH/s of hashrate on a 3.47 TH worker. “A miner of this size has about a one in 1650 chance of solving a block in a year,” Kolivas wrote. The block was tagged to Solo CK on the mempool.space block explorer, and its coinbase carries the pool’s signature. CKpool describes itself as a service that lets miners go after full solo blocks without running their own node, since you cannot mine directly to a Bitcoin Core node. A recent run of solo wins Solo CK has found five blocks since Nov. 6, according to the explorer’s pool page . The most recent before this one was block 976,642 on Nov. 19, followed by blocks on Nov. 11, Nov. 7 and Nov. 6. Each paid between 3.13 and 3.15 BTC. Earlier this year, a different solo miner won block 943,411 on the same service on April 2, for about 3.139 BTC. In October, a FutureBit Apollo solo miner found block 973,262 and earned 3.154 BTC. Those wins are the exception. Most of the network’s hashrate sits in large pools and industrial operations that split rewards across many miners, which is how they smooth out the luck. A single small machine can run for years without finding anything, and a lucky block can show up on day one. Miners on the service get nothing unless they find a block, and then they keep the full reward minus the 2% fee. Network hashrate and difficulty Bitcoin’s network hashrate was about 1.04 zettahashes per second, or roughly 1,043 exahashes, on a three-day average Monday. At 11.1 TH/s, the winning miner contributes about 0.000001% of that total, which fits Kolivas’s odds. One in 1,650 works out to a chance of about 0.06% over a full year of mining. Mining difficulty is about 134.8 trillion. The last adjustment cut it by about 9.1%, and the next one, expected around Nov. 26, is estimated to raise it by about 9.2%, according to mempool.space. item.title: NASA Seeks Partners to Design First Nuclear Reactor for the Moon
item.description: Artist’s concept of a nuclear fission power system on the Moon’s surface. Credit: NASA NASA is seeking industry partners to develop and test the first nuclear reactor designed to provide electricity on the Moon, a major step toward establishing a sustained human presence on the lunar surface. Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1) will be a small fission power system that will generate 20 kilowatts of electricity, enough to power approximately 16 average U.S. households annually on Earth. For NASA’s plans for a Moon Base , that energy could support future habitats, communications systems, rovers, scientific instruments, and other essential infrastructure. NASA aims to have a launch-ready system by 2030 and operate it on the Moon for at least five years after deployment. Unlike solar power, which depends on sunlight, a nuclear reactor can generate electricity continuously, including during the Moon’s approximately two-week-long nights. This capability will enable future lunar operations, particularly in locations where sunlight is limited or unavailable. “This request for proposals represents an important step forward as NASA partners with industry to establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface,” said Brian Giblin, NASA’s Lunar Reactor-1 program manager. “A reliable source of safe and abundant energy will be vital to future exploration of the lunar and Martian surface. Space nuclear systems will provide continuous power to NASA assets in any environment without dependency on sunlight.” NASA’s Space Power and Reactor Capabilities Request for Proposals incorporates feedback received after the agency released a draft proposal in August and hosted an industry day in September at the Ohio Aerospace Institute in Cleveland. The solicitation requires that the reactor must meet Department of Energy (DOE) safety standards for nuclear operations. While the primary purpose of the Request for Proposals is to advance the technology, testing, and flight design of LR-1, NASA may issue additional task orders to support the development of other space nuclear power systems. Proposals are due by Dec. 21. Nuclear power will be increasingly important to NASA’s space exploration ambitions. Lunar nights last about 14 Earth days, while dust storms on Mars can block sunlight for months. Farther from the Sun, solar power becomes progressively less effective. Nuclear systems offer a reliable source of electricity in these challenging environments. LR-1 is managed by the agency’s Space Reactors Division in partnership with the Department of Energy. The division is also responsible for the development of NASA’s Space Reactor‑1 (SR-1) Freedom. Scheduled to launch in 2028, SR-1 Freedom will deliver three SkyFall helicopters to Mars and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion, which uses electricity generated by a nuclear reactor to power spacecraft propulsion systems. It’s a Homecoming! Karan Checker, Temi Nkem and Ashish Checker The entire continent of Africa witnessed the 21-year-old influencer’s genuine love for Checkers Custard during her ten-week stay in Big Brother’s house with the incessant trips to the kitchen primarily to make her favourite snack, in-between meal filler and as a whole meal with select pairings. item.title: Bulgaria evicts cyber snoops who lurked inside government networks for 5 years
item.description: The Ancient Thracian heartland of Bulgaria says it has shut down a cyberespionage operation that gave intruders access to government networks for five years – the longest-running known campaign against its administration. Bulgaria's Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation said the unauthorized and officially unattributed attackers first gained access to infrastructure used by government institutions to exchange information in 2021. It explained that the intrusion went unnoticed for so long because "the previous means of protection did not work as a single, integrated system," and that without a new, recently installed product, it may have gone undetected for much longer. "The incident was discovered thanks to the new national cybersecurity system, which for the first time provides a single picture of what is happening in state networks," the ministry added. "Without it, this activity would most likely have remained hidden for an indefinite period of time." Bulgaria acknowledged that "sensitive information related to the work of the state" was accessed, but did not specify the scale of the compromise. Innovation and Digital Transformation Minister Ivan Vasilev said attackers had downloaded more than 130 GB of data over five years. He also put the volume at 62 million pages. The Register contacted the Bulgarian government for confirmation of these numbers. The ministry said that it has not yet found any evidence that citizens' personal data was compromised, and that the affected infrastructure "will be under increased surveillance for 90 days" in case the attackers try to regain access. Vasilev said multiple international hacking groups had accessed government systems since 2021. He did not specify the names of these groups, however, nor did he name any specific countries that may have been involved. In a follow-up interview with bTV , Vasilev blamed political instability and frequent changes of ministerial leadership for leaving government systems inadequately protected. A representative of the Progressive Bulgaria party, which back in May won Bulgaria's eighth general election in five years, Vasilev said the "constant change of leadership" means "important things for the state do not actually happen." Vasilev said the intrusion was discovered over the summer as the national cybersecurity system was upgraded, and that teams had spent the past three to four months removing the attackers. ®

item.title: Weird 'potato chips' and 'ghostly rocks' on Mars spotted by NASA rovers Curiosity and Perseverance
item.description: null NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance rovers have spotted a bizarre assortment of Martian oddities, from potato chip-like rocks and ghostly white formations to mysterious patterns etched into the Red Planet's surface. While their appearances may be unusual, these formations offer scientists something far more valuable than a collection of curious snapshots: clues to the geological processes that shaped Mars over billions of years. In particular, the rocks and mineral deposits could help researchers piece together the planet's watery past and identify environments that may once have been capable of supporting microbial life. NASA's Curiosity rover recently wrapped up a drilling campaign at a location nicknamed "Nazca," where scientists have been examining unusual disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in the surrounding bedrock. Some of the features are so thin and flat that the mission team likened them to potato chips, according to a statement from the space agency. NASA's Curiosity rover captured a close-up view of unusual, disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in Martian bedrock using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI) on Nov. 7, 2026 (Sol 5067). The thin, flattened formations resemble tiny potato chips. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) Curiosity used its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI), mounted on the end of its robotic arm, to capture detailed close-up images of the formations on Nov. 7 — the rover's 5,067th Martian day , or Sol 5067. The rover also used its ChemCam instrument to study the rocks' chemical composition, while samples from the Nazca drill site were delivered to its onboard Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) instrument for further analysis. Meanwhile, NASA's Perseverance rover has been investigating a collection of unusually bright rocks in an area called "Idubi," located in the “Lac de Charmes” region outside Jezero Crater. The rover captured images of the formations on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023), revealing pale, ghostly-looking rocks that stand out dramatically against the darker, dust-covered Martian landscape. Data from Perseverance's SuperCam instrument revealed that the rocks are rich in hydrated silica rather than being typical igneous rocks. That discovery has scientists particularly interested. On Earth, hydrated silica can form in environments involving hydrothermal activity or groundwater. These deposits are also capable of preserving microscopic fossils, making them valuable targets in the search for evidence of ancient life, according to another statement from NASA. NASA's Perseverance rover captured unusually bright, silica-rich rock in the "Idubi" area outside Jezero Crater on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023), using its left Mastcam-Z camera. The pale formation stands out against the darker, dust-covered Martian terrain. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ASU) Perseverance is now conducting a closer investigation of the formations, using its instruments to gather detailed chemical and mineralogical data that could help scient

item.title: Microsoft mega outage: Report reveals testing gaps and emails that never arrived
item.description: Some emails never reached their recipients during November's Microsoft 365 outage, the company has confirmed in a final report that also exposes gaps in its testing and recovery procedures. The post-incident report details how a Windows defect brought down Exchange Online and disrupted features across other Microsoft 365 services. For affected users, the cloud became someone else's unavailable computer. A preliminary report had already blamed a July code change, combined with a failover and reduced capacity. The final report confirms those findings and sets out Microsoft's plans to improve change auditing and recovery procedures, and add spare capacity. The defect affected Microsoft's gateway server configuration, not standard Windows deployments. The epic outage (named the "Microsoft long weekend" by some wags) kicked off on November 12 and wasn't fully resolved until November 14. Microsoft extended its delivery retry window to 48 hours, but some delayed messages destined for consumer mailboxes inactive for more than 30 days still expired, generating non-delivery reports. The company said all queued enterprise messages were eventually delivered, with none found permanently lost. The report is grim, particularly in how the failure ramped up as US users came online to find gateway servers toppling over. At the worst point, more than 80 percent of North American gateway servers were unresponsive. The problem proved elusive, and it took Microsoft some time to identify the change and deploy a fix. Microsoft has had a week to ponder what it did and did not do, and the report has some next steps to avoid a repeat of November's events. Some are obvious, and some are a little surprising. Working to reduce the blast radius of failures is an obvious one, and actions include partitioning and isolation to ensure failures can be contained before taking down traffic globally. Recovery procedures also need improvement, along with communication and capacity to ensure there is sufficient headroom. Microsoft's load tests used older, lower-core-count hardware, making them less likely to expose a defect that worsened on newer machines. The company now plans to test newer hardware with more realistic traffic and peak loads, and broaden its failover testing. Microsoft also plans to improve diagnostics and change auditing so engineers can identify troublesome Windows changes faster. July's defect had been running worldwide for more than three months before it brought the gateways down. ®

NASA+ Documentary Captures Europa Clipper’s Journey Into Deep Space
item.description: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) The NASA+ original documentary “The Europa Concept” takes audiences along on the journey to send a spacecraft to Jupiter’s moon Europa to determine whether the ocean beneath the moon’s icy shell has the ingredients for life. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech NASA invites the world behind the scenes to witness the story of Europa Clipper’s journey from a far-off vision to a cutting-edge deep space exploration mission with the release of the agency’s newest documentary, “The Europa Concept.” The documentary will air on NASA+ , the NASA app, and the agency’s website starting Monday, Nov. 23, and is coming soon to YouTube. It took decades of science, thousands of dedicated minds, endless creativity, and a whole lot of grit to get the Europa Clipper spacecraft to the launch pad in 2024. Now the orbiter, the largest NASA has ever sent into deep space, is two years into its five-year, 1.8 billion-mile (2.9 billion-kilometer) journey to the Jupiter system, where it will conduct flybys of Europa in search of the conditions for life in the vast ocean thought to hide beneath the moon’s icy surface. “The things we will learn from Europa Clipper will be so sensational, so fantastic, that everyone will be screaming for the next mission,” said Curt Niebur, program scientist in the Planetary Science Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. “The only thing that matters is that we learn enough that we, in the broadest sense, want to do it again somewhere else — because that’s what exploration is.” Following a team of dedicated engineers and scientists on their yearslong efforts, the documentary captures how they developed a mission to Europa and built a spacecraft capable of surviving one of the most punishing radiation environments in our solar system. A product of Jupiter’s powerful magnetic field, that same radiation may have contributed to creating a potentially habitable environment on Europa. The moon, an object of fascination since its discovery by Galileo Galilei in 1610, only began to reveal its secrets with data obtained by NASA’s Pioneer 10 in 1973, followed the next year by Pioneer 11. But humanity didn’t get its first detailed look at Europa until Voyager 1’s flyby in 1979. More detailed glimpses of the moon followed from the agency’s Voyager 2, Galileo, Cassini, and Juno missions, each helping illuminate the way for Europa Clipper. Work officially began on the mission at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California in 2013, initiating an 11-year trek to build the spacecraft and its suite of nine science instruments in time to launch during a specific period of planetary alignment. Along the way, the team encountered plenty of unforeseen challenges, including a global pandemic and, just before launch on Oct. 14, 2024, a Category 5 hurricane and tornadoes near NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. “With Europa Clipper, we’ve taken the next step in solar system explo

item.title: Nvidia Soars as Huang Returns, Lifting Stocks and Crypto Shares
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Nvidia Soars as Huang Returns, Lifting Stocks and Crypto Shares Nvidia shares jumped about 35% on Monday after the chipmaker reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, restoring roughly $1 trillion in market value at the open. The stock traded near $169.20 at 10:41 a.m. ET, up from Friday’s close of $125.53, and Wall Street rallied with it. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back, effective immediately, after what it called a series of discussions and meetings. It said it received input from “senior levels of the United States government” and is confident his return “poses no national security risk.” President Donald Trump had urged the move. Several items remain open. An independent board committee will finish its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, and Huang said he will cooperate. Nvidia also formed a national security and export control committee and is searching for a chief compliance officer. From resignation to reversal Huang resigned on Nov. 11, days after admitting an affair with a woman U.S. officials believe is linked to Chinese intelligence. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress became interim CEO and Harvey Jones became board chair. Nvidia had said it was searching for a permanent successor. The stock slid for seven straight weeks, the longest such streak since 2008. On Friday it plunged 14% after Reuters reported that the SEC is examining the company’s accounting practices. Reuters noted that investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing. Huang’s return reverses most of the losses since his affair became public. The selloff came even after Nvidia reported better-than-expected quarterly results on Nov. 17. For weeks, the board had said it was not considering bringing Huang back, which makes Monday’s announcement a sharp turn for the world’s most closely watched chipmaker. Wall Street and chip stocks rally The Nasdaq Composite rose about 7.4% to near 24,300 at 10:41 a.m. ET, and the S&P 500 gained about 5.4% to near 7,280. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed about 3.3%, or more than 1,500 points, to near 49,700. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days. Chip stocks followed Nvidia higher. Micron (MU) rose about 21% and Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) gained about 16%, while Intel (INTC) added about 15%. AMD rose about 9% and Broadcom (AVGO) was up about 3%. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned on Sunday that the Fed may be making a “policy mistake” if it overtightens. The central bank meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point increase remains the base case. Bitcoin and crypto stocks follow The bitcoin price climbed to a Monday high near $64,500, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, and was near $63,000 at 10:41 a.m. ET. That is about $8,000 above the weekend low of $55,106, hit at roughly 1:17 a.m. ET on Saturday. Bitcoin had slid with stocks on Friday. Crypto-linked stocks jumped. item.description: Nvidia's board of directors has voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman of the board, just 11 days after he resigned in the wake of multiple scandals . The reinstatement, announced Monday morning , is "effective immediately" and was based in part on "input from senior levels of the United States government" that assured the board members that "Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk." That assurance comes despite Huang's admitted affair with a woman who, US intelligence sources believe, was working as a Chinese spy and allegations that Nvidia had subverted export controls meant to keep Nvidia chips from reaching China.
