item.title: The view from the tower: Watch Starship come in for chopsticks catch in epic slo-mo video
item.description: null A new set of slo-mo videos gives us a new perspective on SpaceX's first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage. The company notched the milestone on Saturday (Nov. 14), when the launch tower at its Starbase site in South Texas caught Starship's Ship spacecraft with its "chopstick" arms. You've probably seen photos and videos showing the epic snag from afar. But on Tuesday (Nov. 17), SpaceX released up-close views — a series of four slo-mo videos captured by cameras near the top of the 480-foot-tall (146 meters) tower. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) "The Starbase tower chopsticks catching their first Starship. This unique architecture was designed for full and rapid reusability, enabling repeat launches and landings from the same pad," SpaceX wrote in a Tuesday X post that shared the videos, a compilation of which you can see embedded above. Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. Its current "V3" version stands about 408 feet (124 m) tall, and future iterations will be even larger . As SpaceX noted in Tuesday's post, the megarocket is also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first for an orbital launch system. The company plans to catch both Starship stages — Ship and the Super Heavy booster — at the launch tower, a recovery strategy designed to enable efficient inspection, refurbishment and reflight. Another view of the chopsticks catch on Nov. 14. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX planned to carry out such a double catch on this most recent test flight , Starship's 15th to date, which launched on Friday evening (Nov. 13). But Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel warning during its return to Starbase about 6.5 minutes after launch and autonomously diverted to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico. That wasn't a huge deal for SpaceX, as it had already caught Super Heavy on three previous test flights . Snagging Ship is tougher; the upper stage returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter than the booster does. SpaceX had not even attempted a Ship catch before Flight 15. But the company managed to pull off the maneuver on its first try. And Ship did some work in orbit before coming home: It deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites on Flight 15, the second batch that the company has sent to low Earth orbit . The first set was deployed on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28.

item.title: Raye Tops the 2027 Grammy Nominations With 11 Including Album of the Year
item.description: Raye singing on stage with her band and backing vocalists. Photo Credit: Raye/Instagram When the 2027 Grammy nominations dropped earlier this week, one name sat right at the top of the entire board: Raye . Out of every artist in the running for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, she has the highest Grammy nominations this year with 11 nods, putting her ahead of Rosalía on nine. If you have been watching her rise over the past few years, seeing her command this much spotlight on music’s biggest stage feels well earned, especially for readers following global talent with Ghanaian roots through her mother’s side of the family. Her reaction online captured just how surreal the moment felt, writing on Instagram: “WHAT IS HAPPENING WHAT IS HAPPENING 11 GRAMMY NOMINATIONS INCLUDING ALBUM OF THE YEAR MY HEARTTTTT CANNOT EVEN FATHOM, MY HEARTTTTTTTT ” before following up with a simple “can’t stop crying .” Raye at home with her parents following the 2027 Grammy nominations announcement. Photo Credit: Raye/Instagram In case you are still catching up on her story, Raye was born Rachel Keen in London to a Ghanaian-Swiss mother and an English father, and she has spent years building a reputation as a sharp songwriter, vocalist, and arranger who refuses to stay boxed into one sound. Many listeners first got to know her through chart-topping collaborations and pop hooks before she parted ways with her former major label to release music independently, taking full creative control of her catalogue and storytelling. That independent leap paid off massively—her album This Music May Contain Hope topped the UK chart in March 2026 and won the 2026 Mercury Prize in October, turning her into one of the most talked-about voices in music. Artwork for This Music May Contain Hope. Photo Credit: Raye/Instagram Her 11 nominations for 2027 stretch right across her artistry, from songwriting and performance to arrangement, visuals, and full-length projects. This Music May Contain Hope is competing in both Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album, while her hit “ WHERE IS MY HUSBAND! “—which reached UK No. 1 in January 2026—is up for Record of the Year, Song of the Year, and Best Pop Solo Performance. She also earned nods for “ Click Clack Symphony ” alongside Hans Zimmer in Best Pop Duo/Group Performance, Best Arrangement, Instrumental and Vocals, and Best Music Video, plus “ Life Boat ” in Best Dance Pop Recording, “ I Hate the Way I Look Today” in Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance, and a Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical nod. Raye holding a number one award following a year of UK chart milestones, including “WHERE IS MY HUSBAND!” hitting No. 1 in January 2026 and This Music May Contain Hope topping the UK chart in March 2026. Photo Credit: Raye/Instagram This is not her first time on the Grammy radar, though it is easily her biggest moment yet. item.title: No more asteroid landing: Engine trouble forces Japan's Hayabusa2 probe to change plans
item.description: null Japan's space agency has decided to switch destinations and objectives for the final act of its Hayabusa2 mission, due to the spacecraft suffering trouble with its ion thrusters. The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft launched back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu . Since delivering the samples to Earth in December 2020 via a reentry capsule, the main spacecraft has been conducting an extended mission of exploration and in July made a super-close flyby of the two-headed asteroid Torifune. But Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end. The spacecraft was scheduled to rendezvous with, and attempt to land on, the tiny, 36-foot-wide (11 meters) near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031, but trouble with the aging spacecraft's engines has forced a change of plan. But Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end. The spacecraft was scheduled to rendezvous with, and attempt to land on, the tiny, 36-foot-wide (11 meters) near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031, but trouble with the aging spacecraft's engines has forced a change of plan. The spacecraft will instead target 2015 BM510, another tiny asteroid. And there will be no landing: Hayabusa2 is scheduled to make a high-speed flyby of the near-Earth object in April 2028. The decision was announced at a Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) press conference on Tuesday (Nov. 17), a day after a Cabinet Office space policy subcommittee meeting. The final functioning thruster out of Hayabusa2's four ion engines suffered a malfunction in mid-August, according to JAXA officials, while a sensor detected unexpected erosion of the spacecraft's surface during its long voyage in space. "The deterioration of the onboard equipment ... is becoming increasingly evident," Japan Times quoted Yuya Mimasu, team leader of the extended mission, as saying. A size comparison between asteroid Ryugu, which was visited by Hayabusa2 in 2020, and its planned next target, 1998 KY26. The 2031 visit to 1998 KY26 is now off, however; Hayabusa2 will instead fly by a different small asteroid in 2028. (Image credit: ESO/M. Kornmesser. Asteroid models: T. Santana-Ros, JAXA/University of Aizu/Kobe University) Despite losing the opportunity to land on KY26, the Hayabusa2 mission has been a huge success for JAXA, and the new direction promises its own intrigues. Asteroid 2015 BM510 has already attracted interest; it's the primary target of a proposal for the European Space Agency 's mini-Fast mission series. Scientists describe the body as a D-type asteroid, meaning it's thought to be organic-rich and comet-like, and may have originated in the outer solar system. Around the same time as Hayabusa2 conducts its high-speed flyby in April 2028, JAXA is also scheduled to launch its next asteroid mission, Destiny+. item.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
item.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. Days in Kigali easily revolve around specialty coffee shops, contemporary art at Inema Arts Center, and a sobering, essential visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial before you head out into the countryside. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. Mauritius Sometimes a proper Christmas break calls for leaving mainland schedules behind altogether for turquoise lagoons, catamaran cruises, and mountain trails. In Mauritius, you can base yourself around Grand Baie in the north for boat trips to Île aux Cerfs and lively beachside dinners, or head south-west toward Le Morne Brabant for coastal hikes and water sports. Between beach days, the bustling Central Market in Port Louis, the lush trails of Black River Gorges National Park, and Casela Nature Parks keep a week-long itinerary full without ever feeling hectic. item.title: China rolls out rocket for launch of 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station (video)
item.description: null China's space station is set to receive its first foreign astronaut. A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov. 17), with launch expected in the next week. The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV). China rolls out the Long March 2F rocket for its Shenzhou-24 astronaut mission on Nov. 17, 2026. (Image credit: CCTV) China's human spaceflight agency, CMSA, stated that all facilities and equipment at the launch site are in good condition, adding that the launch is scheduled to take place in the coming days, without providing a date. CMSA typically holds a press conference at Jiuquan a day ahead of launch, during which the crew for the mission is revealed to the public. This time, one of the three crew members will, for the first time, be an international astronaut. One of two Pakistani astronaut candidates will fly to the Tiangong space station on Shenzhou-24, marking a first both for China's outpost and for Pakistan, which will see one its astronauts reach orbit for the first time. Though public details are sparse, it is thought that the Pakistani astronaut, operating as a payload specialist, will stay aboard Tiangong for around a week, returning home on the departing Shenzhou-23 spacecraft. One of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts — who are approaching the end of their six-month-long mission, having launched on May 24 — will stay aboard Tiangong for another half a year. This will provide the international visitor with a seat home on Shenzhou-23, and allow a Chinese astronaut to make the country's first year-long stay in orbit. This extra-long mission will supply China with data on physiology ahead of crewed lunar flights and other long-duration missions. China approved its human spaceflight program in 1992 and launched its first orbital crewed mission in 2003, with Yang Liwei becoming the first Chinese national in space. The country then completed the three-module Tiangong space station in late 2022 and has kept the orbital outpost constantly crewed ever since, with rotating six-month-long missions with brief handovers between crews. Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed mission and will mark the first time a foreign national is flying on a Shenzhou spacecraft. China is also looking to double the size of Tiangong in the coming years, potentially opening the way to further international missions and space tourist visits.

item.title: Don't miss Saturn shine close to the moon tonight
item.description: null The moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset tonight (Nov. 20), presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby. Saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length. Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky. The moon will present a spectacular target through the eyepiece of a 6-inch telescope, as the terminator line separating night from day creeps ever closer to its western edge. It's a great time to explore the 110 km-wide Gassendi Crater on the edge of Mare Humorum as its eastern rim and central peaks throw intense shadows across its interior. Gassendi Crater is a fascinating target for telescope observation during the moon's waxing gibbous phase. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva. Inset: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio.) Slewing your telescope over to Saturn will reveal details and subtle variations in the cloud surface of the gas giant , along with its iconic ring system, which is gradually becoming more visible following its ring plane crossing in March 2025. Depending on viewing conditions, you may also notice a shoal of bright, star-like points of light surrounding Saturn's disk, which represent the large moons Titan , Dione , Tethys , Rhea and Iapetus . Interested in seeing the planets of the solar system up close for yourself? Then be sure to check out our picks of the best telescopes available in 2026 , including the Celestron NexStar 8SE , which we rate as the best motorized scope out there. Editor's Note: If you would like to share your planetary astrophotography with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: Netflix's '3 Body Problem' season 2 trailer gives us a release date and a chilling warning: 'They are coming to exterminate us'
item.description: null " 3 Body Problem ," Netflix's unsettling adaptation of the first book in Chinese author Cixin Liu's epic alien invasion trilogy, "Remembrance of Earth’s Past," made a serious impact on viewers searching for hardcore E.T. drama and now an explosive new trailer for season 2 has just entered our orbit. This sensational saga about a malevolent interstellar society trying to exist within the unpredictable orbital mechanics of a planet and its triple sun system that forms an Earth-bound armada still has us a bit slack-jawed more than two years after debuting in 2024 . Now we're admittedly eager for this shortened 6-episode sophomore outing, which is officially arriving on Jan. 14, 2027. Delivered by Emmy Award-winning "Game of Thrones" team of David Benioff and D.B. Weiss and "True Blood's" Alexander Woo, "3 Body Problem" season 2 revolves around the combined forces of the Planetary Defense Council as they mount a daring deep space counterattack against the San-Ti. The San-Ti have arrived in Netflix's "3 Body Problem" season 2! (Image credit: Netflix) These Trisolarians are not the friendliest of galactic neighbors, and prior to the all-out invasion their primary goal was to thwart humanity’s ability to create advanced defense weaponry in the four centuries it would take for them to enter our solar system. This time it's more about the next phase of ultimate survival and dire actions taken by anti-alien and pro-alien factions. Season 2 leaps forward 400 years and focuses on the results of the Wallfacer Project, a secret initiative where chosen individuals worked on solutions in isolation as to not attract the attention of the Trisolarian's omnipresent AI surveillance technology called sophons. While the debut season was based on Liu's Hugo Award-winning 2008 novel, "The Three-Body Problem," this upcoming Netflix offering will adapt the second book, "The Dark Forest." 2010's "Death's End" closed out the acclaimed sci-fi trilogy. Netflix Netflix Netflix Netflix "So much of season 1 is about the mystery of what's happening," co-creator and co-executive producer David Benioff tells Netflix. "By the time season 2 starts, we have a lot more information. We know there is a hostile alien civilization out there, the San-Ti, and they’re coming our way, and they want our planet for themselves." Landing on Jan. 14, 2027, "3 Body Problem" season 2's international cast includes returners Jess Hong, Benedict Wong, Jovan Adepo, Eiza González, Liam Cunningham, Marlo Kelly, Sea Shimooka, Saamer Usmani, Alex Sharp and Josh Brener. Joining them are fresh cast members Claudia Doumit, Ellie de Lange, Alfie Allen, David Yip and Jordan Sunshine. item.title: Empire State Building glows gold for NASA's Voyager spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 19, 2026
item.description: null The Empire State Building is illuminated in gold to celebrate Voyager 1 hitting one light-day from Earth, seen here on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, from SUMMIT One Vanderbilt in New York City. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov. 17) to celebrate NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hitting one light-day from Earth. And it isn't the only building celebrating this achievement with a sparkling display. What is it? Today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth. About 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) away, this is the point at which it takes a full day (or 24 hours) for one light particle to get from us to the probe. So any signal we send to Voyager 1 or it sends back now takes a full day as the spacecraft continues to explore interstellar space. To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in New York City lit up in gold . This golden glow references the Golden Record onboard both the Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft. And the Empire State Building wasn't the only major landmark to celebrate the occasion. The Space Needle in Seattle, Washington, and both the Willis Tower and the Skydeck Chicago in Chicago, Illinois have all been illuminated gold to mark the milestone. Why is it incredible? The Golden Record that these gold glowing buildings are referencing serves as an inanimate ambassador for Earth , carrying information about humanity, our planet, the other species who live here, the languages we speak, the music we listen to and so much more. It even includes instructions for building a record player to play the record. The Voyager mission has, and continues to, make incredible scientific discoveries and observations throughout our solar system and now in interstellar space. But this Golden Record provides an additional aspect to the mission that connects us here on Earth to whatever unknown life may exist out there. If some sort of life forms out in the cosmos were to ever come across Voyager and its Golden Record at any point in the distant future, they might learn a little bit about our small blue dot.

item.title: Leonid meteor shower thrills stargazers worldwide with colorful sky show (photos/video)
item.description: null The Leonid meteor shower put on quite the show this week, with bright, colorful meteors thrilling stargazers worldwide and we've got the photos to prove it. The annual meteor shower peaked overnight on Nov. 17-18, with photographers braving chilly temperatures, clouds and even fog in hopes of catching the perfect shot. And for some, their patience certainly paid off. Leonids occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. As tiny pieces of comet debris enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of up to 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up, producing bright streaks of light. The meteor shower is also famous for producing some of the most spectacular meteor storms in history. In fact, this year marks the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, when observers reported an astonishing 40 meteors per second at the peak. To mark the occasion, we spoke to people who witnessed the extraordinary event first-hand and you can read their remarkable accounts in our special feature . But back to the present! Let's take a look at some of the best photographs and videos captured during this year's impressive display. Photographer Austin Rebello drove several hours to Nubble Lighthouse in York, Maine, to meet up with fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright and hopefully capture a Leonid or two. "I specifically drove a few hours up there for hopes of capturing exactly this, as the radiant of the Leonids rose behind the lighthouse," Rebello told Space.com in an email. Leonid meteor streaks over Nubble Lighthouse, York, Maine. (Image credit: Austin Rebello) "My friend and I were lucky enough to also see it with our eyes, and it was definitely a top 3 meteor for me, as it was even bright enough to briefly cast shadows." A close up view of a Leonid meteor. (Image credit: Austin Rebello) Rebello also revealed on X that the meteor left behind a vibrant blue trail that remained visible to the naked eye for more than 30 seconds. The meteor left a vibrant blue streak that was visible to the naked eye for more than 30 seconds. (Image credit: Austin Rebello) Fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright was also at Nubble Lighthouse that night, where he captured the lingering trail of a particularly bright meteor on camera for an incredible 12 minutes, according to a post on X. "Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there," Wright wrote on X . Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there. I was able to make a rough timelapse video to show this.--November 18, 2026York, Maine https://t.co/pm9htHcMm3 November 18, 2026 This phenomenon is known as a persistent meteor train and is created when a bright meteor leaves behind a trail of ionized gas that continues to glow long after the meteor itself has disappeared. item.title: Nonprofit Common Space will launch 1st 'humanitarian satellite' in 2027
item.description: null The first satellite in a constellation designed for humanitarian use will lift off next year, if all goes according to plan. The nonprofit Common Space plans to assemble a six-spacecraft constellation of Earth-observing satellites , whose high-resolution imagery will aid first responders, journalists, scientists and human-rights investigators around the world. That plan firmed up a bit today (Nov. 19), as Common Space announced the builder of the first of those satellites : Satellogic, an Argentine-U.S. geospatial intelligence company. There are more than 1,000 Earth-observing satellites circling our planet at the moment. But much of the data they gather is proprietary or too expensive to serve the common good, according to Common Space. The nonprofit wants to change that via its envisioned constellation, which it says will collect imagery specifically for humanitarian and public-interest purposes. Common Space plans to operate on a "club-good model," which will share infrastructure and costs across a large community, allowing extensive, low-cost access to high-quality imagery. Satellogic is now officially part of this picture. "With Satellogic as our spacecraft partner, we're moving from vision to orbit and putting high-resolution data into the hands of those who need it most," Common Space co-founder Rhiannan Price said in a statement today. "This isn't just another satellite. We're building infrastructure to serve people for years to come." The satellite is Satellogic's NewSat Mark V, which Common Space selected after a competitive request-for-proposal process. Satellites can help first responders deal with natural disasters. Here, one of Vantor's Earth-imaging satellites captures the destruction Hurricane Melissa caused to Black River, in southwest Jamaica, in November 2025. (Image credit: Vantor Technologies/CC BY 4.0) The NewSat Mark V is just 32 inches (82 centimeters) long and weighs 85 pounds (38.5 kilograms) here on Earth . But the microsatellite packs a great deal of capability into that small package. From low Earth orbit (LEO), it naturally resolves features on the ground as small as 27.5 inches (70 cm), which Satellogic's proprietary algorithms can boost to a "super resolution" of 19.7 inches (50 cm). The satellite is scheduled to launch in July 2027, on a rocket that has yet to be announced. Satellogic will handle the preparations for that launch and manage satellite operations, which are expected to last at least five years in LEO. The company has extensive experience with such work; it has flown 61 of its Earth-observing satellites to date, all of which deployed successfully. And Satellogic is aligned with Common Space philosophically, the company stressed. "Common Space shares our belief that persistent global intelligence shouldn't be reserved for a few. Humanitarian responders and journalists are often first on the ground and last to get access, yet they need frequent, high-resolution imagery to see what's really happenin

item.title: Parents: please don’t buy Grand Theft Auto VI for your child
item.description: Rockstar Games’ brilliant 18-rated criminal caper is stuffed with sex, drugs and violence. It is the most explicit game I’ve ever played – and it really is not for kids Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI? I am haunted still by an interaction I had at my stepson’s ninth birthday party in 2014, where one of the kids asked if I could put on Grand Theft Auto V for them all. “I have it at home!”, he said, giving me the puppy-dog eyes. Mentally replaying that game in my head, flashing back to the many scenes involving such things as smoking meth, over-the-top gratuitous violence and grubby sex in one character’s trailer, I said “ no way” . Later I gently mentioned to the kid’s mother that GTA V was an 18-rated game and really wasn’t suitable for kids. “Oh, but he’s really good at these games,” she told me. She was genuinely shocked to learn that an 18-rating on a video game was a flag for adult content, rather than an indication of its difficulty. Grand Theft Auto VI is released this week. It is an incredible creative and technical feat, conjuring a realistic-looking and exhaustively detailed virtual Florida filled with every kind of filth and criminality you could imagine. It is brilliant, entertainingly observed and even sometimes unexpectedly touching, largely thanks to a central love story between the player couple , Jason and Lucia. It is lewd, violent and frequently hilarious. It is also absolutely full of stuff that I really would not want my 10 and seven-year-old boys to see or hear. I have never played a game that has more thoroughly earned its 18 rating. Continue reading...

item.title: From Tunde Kelani to Akinola Davies Jr., 5 Nollywood Directors You Should Know
item.description: From music visuals to international festival stages and actor-turned-director debuts, Dammy Twitch, Akinola Davies Jr., and Daniel Etim Effiong represent different paths into Nollywood directing. Think about the Nigerian films and series you have watched recently, the ones that kept you glued to your screen, had you talking about the storyline long after the credits rolled or recommending them to everyone you know. While the actors are often the faces you remember first, there is someone behind the camera whose creative choices help bring those stories to life: the director. From interpreting the script and guiding actors to shaping how each scene looks, sounds and unfolds, directors influence almost every part of what ends up on screen. As Nollywood grows in ambition, production quality and global reach, the filmmakers steering these projects are becoming just as central to the industry’s story as the stars in front of the lens. Some have spent decades bringing Nigerian literature and history to the screen, while others are earning international acclaim or crossing over from music videos into feature films. Here are five Nollywood directors whose work is worth knowing. Tunde Kelani Start with Tunde Kelani if you want to see where modern Nigerian cinema found its literary and cultural roots. Trained at the London Film School after cutting his teeth in photography and television, the Mainframe Films founder has spent decades turning Nigerian literature, stage plays, and history into lasting screen works. Titles like Ti Oluwa Nile , Koseegbe , O Le Ku , Saworoide , Thunderbolt: Magun , The Narrow Path , Maami , Dazzling Mirage , Ayinla , and Cordelia show how wide his range goes. Across years of festivals and awards, Kelani has collected major honours for his craft, and his adaptation Cordelia earned him a Best Director nomination at the 2026 Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards. Tunde Kelani, whose directing catalogue spans Ti Oluwa Nile, Saworoide, The Narrow Path, Maami, and Cordelia, with Kunle Afolayan outdoors. Photo Credit: Tunde Kelani/Instagram Akinola Davies Jr. Few directors have linked global festival stages with homegrown Nollywood triumphs quite like Akinola Davies Jr. After his short film Lizard won the Short Film Grand Jury Prize at the Sundance Film Festival in 2021, he co-wrote and directed his feature debut My Father’s Shadow alongside his brother Wale Davies . The drama made history in 2025 as the first Nigerian film selected for the Official Selection at the Cannes Film Festival, picking up a Special Mention for the Caméra d’Or before winning Best Director at the British Independent Film Awards and Breakthrough Director at the Gotham Independent Film Awards. His momentum rolled straight into 2026 with a BAFTA win for Outstanding Debut by a British Writer, Director or Producer, followed by Best Director and Best Overall Movie wins at the 2026 AMVCAs. Akinola Davies Jr. with his BAFTA trophy for My Father’s Shadow. Photo Credit: A

item.title: What's next for NASA interstellar Voyager 1 probe after passing 1 light-day from Earth?
item.description: null Voyager 1 has reached a historic milestone in space — it now takes a light-day to send a command to the spacecraft, meaning a full 24 hours for Earth to hail the distant spacecraft. Since Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2 , launched on an initial tour through the outer solar system in 1977, their missions have been packed with science. Voyager 1 looked at Jupiter and Saturn from up close before veering for a flyby of Saturn's moon Titan and Saturn's rings, a pathway that brought it above the plane of the solar system in the early 1980s. Voyager 1's faster path out of the solar system brought it to one light-day in distance on Wednesday (Nov. 18), while Voyager 2 — which took a slightly slower track to see Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune — will reach a light-day of distance in 2035. So what's next for the two Voyager spacecraft as they reach further into interstellar space? Exploring afar Interstellar space, which is the area where the sun's constant stream of solar particles within the heliopause gives way to the physics of interstellar space, has been a valuable harvest for both Voyagers. Voyager 1 crossed interstellar space in August 2012 and continues to get data, while Voyager 2 has done the same since November 2018. "Current science is continuing our investigation on magnetic field strength and direction, plasma density, and energetic particle detection. What is important is to measure how these phenomena change as the spacecraft travels further away from the sun," Suzanne Dodd, project manager for the Voyager missions at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), told Space.com in an email. Added to that will be the Voyagers' examinations of plasma and magnetic fields nearby the spacecraft, and a focus on any "solar effects" such as shocks or pressure fronts, added JPL project scientist Linda Spilker in an email. "Key Voyager science going forward includes observing the extent to which our sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1," Spilker continued. "Where does the sun's influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may last long enough to answer that question." The team also wants to watch the magnetic field around the spacecraft continue to change direction from the sun, to interstellar space, Spilker noted. That finding was not expected when the Voyagers launched, so scientists are curious to know more — as long as the spacecraft can last, that is. The locations of Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 beyond the boundary of our solar system. (Image credit: NASA, ESA, and Z. Levay (STScI)) Power management Each Voyager continues to lose 4 watts of power a year; their launch power was 470 watts in 1977, and the nuclear power source continues to dwindle, requiring harder choices as the missions approach their 50th years of operations. item.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
item.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. The Empty Chair Nobody Notices This year’s theme for International Men’s Day, celebrated on November 19th, is “The Future Is Everyone.” While this theme may seem straightforward, it invites us to explore the true meaning of “everyone.” Working in corporate communications at the Chartered Institute of Personnel Management of Nigeria (CIPM) has heightened my awareness of how easily we categorise people based on their roles: leaders, em

item.title: Burna Boy, Asake & Seyi Vibez Bring Afrobeats to the World of GTA VI
item.description: From left: Nigerian artists Asake, Seyi Vibez, and Burna Boy, whose songs appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. How else could Grand Theft Auto VI begin than with Nigerian artists featured in the music lineup of the biggest video game release of the year? As players around the world finally step into Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated open-world action-adventure title, Burna Boy , Asake , and Seyi Vibez are making sure Nigerian music is front and centre on the virtual streets of Vice City and the wider state of Leonida. Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) officially arrives today, Thursday, 19 November 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, ending a 13-year wait since Grand Theft Auto V first hit consoles. Developed and published by Rockstar Games, the open-world action-adventure game follows dual protagonists Jason and Lucia across the sun-soaked, neon-lit state of Leonida—a fictional take on Florida that brings players back to Vice City in the franchise’s largest map yet. Music has always been at the heart of the Grand Theft Auto universe, where players tune into curated in-game radio stations while driving or walking around town, and this sixth instalment takes African soundscapes seriously. At the centre of the Nigerian presence is AfroBank FM, a dedicated African music radio station inside Grand Theft Auto VI that is co-hosted by Grammy winner Burna Boy—credited on-air simply as Burna—alongside British DJ and producer Palms Trax , who goes by Palmsy. Curated to spotlight everything from 20th-century African classics to contemporary Afrobeats, amapiano, and 3-step, the station features Asake’s 2022 hit “ Joha ” from his debut album Mr Money With The Vibe , as well as “ Giza “, the 2023 collaboration between Burna Boy and Seyi Vibez from Burna Boy’s seventh studio album I Told Them …. Alongside those tracks, Burna Boy also appears on the game’s official companion soundtrack album, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, with his original song “ Bigger ” sitting on a 34-track roster that includes Travis Scott , Cardi B , Dua Lipa , SZA , Tame Impala , and Lana Del Rey . The African representation on AfroBank FM stretches beyond Nigeria too, sharing airwaves with Ghanaian highlife legends Pat Thomas and Ebo Taylor on “ Gye Wani ” and South African stars DJ Lag , Robot Boii , and Kamo Mphela on “ Shay’sana “. With players able to listen to Leonida’s terrestrial radio stations both in vehicles and on foot through in-game headphones, millions of gamers worldwide are now cruising through Vice City with Burna Boy on the mic and Asake and Seyi Vibez on heavy rotation. The post Burna Boy, Asake & Seyi Vibez Bring Afrobeats to the World of GTA VI appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: How La Roche-Posay Brought Skin Science to Over 500 Guests in Its First Living Lab Experience
item.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. The film also highlighted how Lipikar supports the care of skin affected by scarring, bringing attention to the importance of addressing both the visible and less visible experiences associated with skin conditions. The programme also created opportunities for visitors to engage with skincare experts and dermatologists through one-on-one consultations, ask questions about their individual skin concerns and receive guidance on building appropriate skincare routines. item.title: The Future Awards Africa (TFAA) celebrates 20 Years of African Excellence with Historic Awards Ceremony
item.description: A historic hosting line-up spanning five African countries and a first-of-its-kind AI assistant named Infinity set the stage for a distinctive celebration as The Future Awards Africa (TFAA) marked its 20th edition on Saturday, 14 November 2026. Held at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, the ceremony brought together young achievers, industry leaders and public figures to celebrate two decades of recognizing African excellence. Themed “ Celebrating the Redefiners: Africa’s AI Generation,” the evening honoured young Africans aged 18 to 35 across 26 categories, including technology and innovation, entrepreneurship, governance, music, film, literature, advocacy, sports and fashion. Their achievements formed the heart of a milestone edition that celebrated the platform’s legacy while embracing new possibilities for its stage. The event was hosted by Nigerian actress and trained lawyer Genoveva Umeh; Claudia Naisabwa , a Kenyan media personality and host; Priscilla Kayira , a Malawian radio broadcaster and television personality; Resego Motlhokathari , a television and radio host from Botswana; and Idris Sultan , a Tanzanian actor and former Big Brother Africa winner. Together, the five hosts gave the anniversary celebration a distinctly continental presence. Bringing different voices, personalities and perspectives to the proceedings, the line-up reflected the reach of an awards platform whose story has grown alongside the generations of young Africans it recognises. The hosts also shared the spotlight with Infinity , an AI assistant that introduced another dimension to the evening. With a distinct voice, quick wit, and playful responses, Infinity engaged with the hosts, drawing laughter and creating unexpected, exciting moments throughout the ceremony. Its appearance offered an exciting glimpse into how artificial intelligence is influencing not only the way people work and create, but also how audiences experience entertainment. Sharp Band and the Loud Urban Choir also entertained guests with captivating musical performances, adding to the evening’s celebratory atmosphere. At the heart of the celebration were the winners and the work that earned them recognition. Nora Awolowo received the Prize for Young Person of the Year, Teniola Aladese won the Prize for Acting, and Olamidun Ogundoyin took home the Prize for Entrepreneurship. Pastor Jerry Uchechukwu Eze , who was represented at the ceremony by media personality Hero Daniels , received the Prize for Service to Young People. The ceremony welcomed representatives of distinguished public figures, including Hon. Mobolaji Abubakre Ogunlende, Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, who represented the Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu . item.title: International Men’s Day: Six Films That Explore the Vulnerable Side of Men
item.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Where does responsibility begin, and where does it end? Do men matter? Do their feelings matter? The theme for this year’s International Men’s Day is “The Future Is For Everyone.” For that, here are some movies that explore and illuminate the complexities of masculinity: The Pursuit of Happyness This classic film reveals the vulnerability often hidden behind male perseverance. Will Smith ’s portrayal of Chris Gardner challenges the stoic notion of manhood by showing fatherhood as both an act of love and endurance. Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. Fatherhood Kevin Hart ’s film Fatherhood delves into themes of grief and single parenthood, balancing humour with heartfelt moments. It challenges traditional expectations of masculinity by illustrating a father’s journey through uncertainty, learning empathy, and committing to being present for his child/ren. Through this film, Kevin Hart shares his vision of what it means to be a man and a father. Adolescence Adolescence examines how boys internalise distorted notions of strength and freedom, and how escaping them demands emotional awareness. The film reveals the journey of a young boy on the brink of adulthood, revealing the pressures of identity and self-definition. There is a lot to unpack from Stephen Graham’ s Adolescence about what it means to be a father and a child. King Richard A faction. In the narrative, King Richard shares the stories of Serena and Venus Williams , highlighting discipline and belief as fundamental expressions of a father’s love. item.title: Astronomers witness a star eating its companion in 1st-of-its-kind observation
item.description: null Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean. We need sensitive telescopes monitoring the sky for a long time in order to catch this effect." In December 2025, observations from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope provided the final evidence that allowed researchers to fully reconstruct what happened before, during, and after the merger of a binary star system nicknamed Bao in the Andromeda galaxy. (Image credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Viraj Karambelkar (Columbia), Kishalay De (Columbia); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI); Acknowledgment: DSS, Robert Gendler) In the new study, the researchers investigated a red giant star designated WNTR23bzdiq, which is located about 2.5 million light-years away in the Andromeda galaxy . The star is about seven times heftier and 350 times wider than our own sun . In 2023, using NASA's now-defunct NEOWISE space telescope and the WINTER telescope at Palomar Observatory in California, the scientists noticed that this star was brightening. By analyzing previous records, they found that the red giant had gradually started growing more luminous in 2018. The researchers had previously suggested this brightening potentially occurred because the giant star engulfed a companion star. As this companion spiraled toward the giant's core, it would generate friction, heat and light, explaining the increasing luminosity. Then, near the end of 2025, the astronomers saw a giant eruption of light from this giant star. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope observed the star just 47 days after that eruption, allowing the team to characterize the event in detail. The researchers now propose that this explosion happened when a companion star about 70% the sun's mass rammed into the giant's heart. "I was absolutely flabbergasted when we saw this," Karambelkar said. In the new study, the scientists estimated that the eruption expelled an amount of material equal to about 0.1 to 0.2 times the mass of the sun . "Stars engulfing their companions have been theorized for many decades, and this event provides the first observations of this theoretical prediction," Karambelkar said. Although these findings suggest that two stars — a binary system nicknamed "Bao" — merged into one, "it is not the only possibility," Karambelkar said. item.title: Tunji Olowolafe Wants Ikogosi to Be Nigeria’s Next Destination for Weddings, Retreats and Landmark Celebrations
item.description: Growing up, Tunji Olowolafe ’s parents brought the family to Are-Ekiti every Christmas, and a trip to Ikogosi was compulsory. Decades later, he returned to the warm springs town with family, friends and business partners, “not to take away, but to help build something enduring in Ekiti.” Speaking as Chairman and Chief Launcher of Ikogosi Day 2026, Thanksgiving and Launch of the Oba’s Palace Project, on Saturday, 14 November 2026, the Chancellor of Ekiti State University set out a vision for Ikogosi built on intentional tourism, enterprise and heritage. Dr. Olowolafe said Ikogosi’s task now is to give visitors compelling reasons to come, stay longer and spend across local businesses. He pointed to the recent Ikogosi 17.5km Race, which drew runners from across Nigeria alongside athletes from Ghana, Kenya and Ethiopia, as an example of what happens when private initiative meets local hospitality. He urged the same thinking for lifestyle and executive tourism, with the ambition of making Ikogosi a premier international destination for weddings, milestone birthdays, corporate retreats and landmark gatherings. “Our natural landscape will draw people in. But only the quality of the experience we deliver, through warmth of welcome, impeccable service and attention to detail, will bring them back,” he said. To build that service culture, he called for a deeper, structured partnership between the Ikogosi Resort and the Hospitality Management Technology Department of the Federal Polytechnic, Ado-Ekiti, which has already produced two sets of National Diploma graduates. The goal is for students to train alongside seasoned professionals while serving real guests. He also proposed alliances with leading international hospitality institutes to benchmark local teaching and service, noting that world-class hospitality must become Ekiti’s signature. He argued that the same commercial discipline must apply to the resources beneath the ground. “It is not enough to say we have clay or kaolin. We must ask: What are their exact industrial specifications? What can we competitively manufacture? And who is ready to buy?” he said. He tasked the Department of Geology at Ekiti State University, headed by Professor Yinka Aturamu , with establishing precise data on local deposits and mapping out what it would take to turn them into viable commercial enterprises. For him, the measure of success is what it changes for young people in the community. “For a young person growing up in Ikogosi, the result must be tangible: a marketable skill, a steady job, a supply contract or a thriving enterprise,” he said. He cited Rasheed Sarumi’s Saroafrica Group as proof of what is possible. The group acquired Gossy Warm Springs in 2018 and restored the plant to full production in 2019. Together with its partners, Saroafrica is now investing US$25 million in a manufacturing facility in Ikogosi, which will run on its own 2MW gas-fired power plant. item.title: Miss Universe 2026: Meet the 17 African Queens Representing the Continent
item.description: From left: Miss Universe Democratic Republic of the Congo 2026 Jessi Kalambayi, Miss Universe Namibia 2026 Charene Labuschagne, and Miss Universe Botswana 2026 Dabilo Moses ahead of the 75th Miss Universe finale in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The Miss Universe stage is getting a beautiful dose of African representation this year, with 17 contestants from across the continent making their way to Puerto Rico for the pageant’s 75th edition. And there are plenty of stories to discover among them, from Uganda ’s historic debut to Nigeria ’s Danielle Adewusi , whose journey to the competition comes with a lovely family connection. Taking place in San Juan, Puerto Rico, the Diamond Anniversary edition will bring together 116 contestants from around the world, all hoping to claim the newly unveiled 75th-anniversary crown, The Radiance of an Eternal Legacy. The grand finale is scheduled for Tuesday, 24 November 2026, at the José Miguel Agrelot Coliseum. This year’s show will be hosted by R’Bonney Gabriel , Mario Lopez , Zuri Hall and Dayanara Torres . At the end of the night, reigning Miss Universe 2025 Fátima Bosch of Mexico will pass on her crown to a new winner. Bosch took the title in Thailand last November, ahead of contestants from Thailand, Venezuela, the Philippines and Côte d’Ivoire. For Africa, the road to this year’s competition has come with a few changes. Angola, the Republic of the Congo, South Sudan, Zambia and Zimbabwe were unable to participate due to U.S. travel and visa restrictions, while Côte d’Ivoire, Mauritius, Rwanda and Senegal withdrew from the competition. Still, 17 African countries have contestants in the running, including Uganda, which is making its historic Miss Universe debut. Cameroon, Ethiopia, Kenya, Sierra Leone and Tunisia are among the countries returning to the global stage. Representing Nigeria is 29-year-old medical doctor and women’s health advocate Danielle Adewusi, also known as Danielle Fadeke Adewusi. Her participation adds a special family detail to the story: she won Miss Universe Nigeria 2026 in Lagos, 35 years after her mother, Tonia Okogbenin , represented the country at Miss Universe 1991. From first-time participation to familiar faces returning to the competition, these are the 17 African beauty queens representing the continent at Miss Universe 2026. Dabilo Moses — Botswana Representing Botswana is 26-year-old Dabilo Moses from Gaborone (born in Tutume). A Broadcasting and Journalism student at Limkokwing University of Creative Technology, she previously won Miss Independence Botswana 2022, reached the Top 24 at Miss Supranational 2023 as Botswana’s first-ever entrant, and was appointed Miss Universe Botswana 2026 after finishing as first runner-up in 2025. The gathering brought together some of Nigeria’s leading content creators, filmmakers, advertising professionals and brand executives to explore how digital influence can translate into original intellectual property, sustainable creative businesses and longer-term commercial opportunities. Laditan explained that Woof Studios works across the business and production aspects of content development, including funding and distribution, to help creators take ideas beyond their initial digital formats. “When creators understand a brand’s business objectives, and brands respect the authentic voice a creator has spent years cultivating, we stop simply buying attention and start co-creating stories that matter.” The conversations at PluggedIN also addressed the realities of building sustainable creative businesses. During the creator-focused panel, Kiekie, Craze Clown, Jay On-Air and Winifred Nwania of Zeelicious Food discussed the opportunities and challenges of building careers in the digital space. They explored content ownership, audience engagement, monetisation and the importance of meaningful brand relationships. The discussions reflected an increasingly important question for the industry: How can creators turn the audiences and cultural influence they have built into sustainable businesses? item.title: Ibukun Awosika, Juliet Ibrahim, Bola Adesola & More: Leading Women Take Centre Stage at The Executive Woman Summit 2.0
item.description: What does it really mean to play to win in business and leadership? Beyond earning a seat at the table, it requires more than competence or professional accomplishments. It requires the confidence to own one’s value, the clarity to communicate one’s contributions and the intentionality to build visibility that translates into meaningful influence. These conversations defined The Executive Woman Summit (TEWS) 2.0 , which brought together hundreds of executive women, corporate professionals, entrepreneurs and emerging leaders at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Convened by Bola Matel-Okoh , a dual-qualified attorney (called to both the New York and Nigerian Bars), Executive Coach, Non-Executive Director at Wema Bank, and CEO of BMO Advisory Services , the second edition of the summit was themed Playing to Win: Elevate Your Vision, Value and Visibility. It provided an intentional platform for candid conversations, practical insights and strategic alliances on what it takes for women to advance, lead and thrive in today’s evolving corporate landscape. In her opening address, Matel-Okoh challenged women to rethink how they approach professional visibility, authority and advancement. According to her, competence is merely the baseline; it is not enough if you are unwilling to communicate your value, own your voice and position yourself for higher-stakes opportunities. This philosophy also came through in her cover interview with THISDAY Glitterati ahead of the summit, where she offered a compelling perspective on the distinction between holding a powerful position and exercising genuine influence. “A powerful position gives you formal authority. Influence determines how deeply your leadership shapes people’s thinking, decisions and actions. A title may secure your place in a meeting, but credibility makes people listen,” she explained. She also challenged the assumption that excellent work will automatically speak for itself, encouraging women to communicate their contributions with evidence and confidence. “What problem did you solve? What result did you produce? What changed because of your leadership?” she asked, highlighting the importance of making professional value visible to the decision-makers who influence career progression and boardroom opportunities. “There is no need to diminish your achievements to make others comfortable. You can be gracious and still be clear about the value you bring,” she added. The summit featured a distinguished line-up of women shaping leadership, business, finance, entertainment and corporate governance. Chairman of Ecobank Nigeria, Bola Adesola , and CEO of FS Global Advisory Services, Folake Sanu , delivered keynote addresses, sharing perspectives on leadership, professional growth, boardroom dynamics and navigating the demands of executive life. item.title: Inside the 2026 WIEN Gala & Awards: A Night of Celebration, Powerful Conversations and a New DEI Benchmark
item.description: The Metropolitan Club, Lagos, was transformed into a gathering of some of the most influential names in Nigeria’s energy industry as the Women in Energy Network (WIEN) hosted its 2026 Gala & Awards. Bringing together industry leaders, policymakers, corporate executives and other distinguished guests, the evening marked six years of WIEN’s advocacy for greater representation, inclusion and leadership opportunities for women across the energy value chain. Beyond the glamour, elegant conversations and celebrations, the event carried a clear message: it is time to move beyond conversations about inclusion and focus on measurable progress. The Honourable Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajia Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim , delivered the special address, ably represented by Dr Adedayo Benjamins-Laniyi , Director-General/Chief Executive Officer of the Maryam Babangida National Centre for Women Development . In her address, WIEN President Eyono Fatayi-Williams emphasised that progress must be visible, measurable and sustained. “As we celebrate six years, we also have to ask ourselves an important question: What do the next six years look like? Because we cannot spend the next six years having the same conversations we have had in the last six years. We cannot continue to talk about inclusion without asking what has changed,” Fatayi-Williams challenged the industry. The evening also featured a keynote address by Dr Mutiu Sunmonu (CON) , Chairman of The Sage Centre for Leadership Excellence, who shared perspectives on leadership and the importance of creating opportunities for women to contribute meaningfully to the sector. Six Years of Building Opportunities for Women Reflecting on the organisation’s growth and the realities of navigating the energy sector, WIEN Board of Trustees Chairperson, Dr Cecilia Aqua Umoren , challenged guests to strive for true parity. “In the six years that WIEN has been in existence, we have created more opportunities for women, resulting in numerous appointments and an expanded STEM pipeline. However, progress is not parity; we are ultimately aiming for true parity. We must acknowledge that most leadership positions today are occupied by men, meaning we cannot achieve our objectives without partnering with them to create access. If the room is not created for you, create your own room, set your own table, and be at your own table.” WIEN’s Executive Secretary, Asanimo Omezi , echoed this commitment, highlighting the network’s growth from a collective of 30 women to more than 1,000 members, supported by 30 corporate partners. “We started as a small collective of just 30 women, and today we have grown to over a thousand members with thirty corporate partners. The newly unveiled DEI benchmark will move us from mere conversation to visible accountability. They want solutions that are intuitive, efficient and capable of making daily life easier. Across Africa, rapid urbanisation, changing lifestyles and growing digital adoption are reshaping consumer expectations. Homeowners are increasingly seeking appliances that combine convenience, performance, energy efficiency and intelligent functionality while fitting seamlessly into their everyday routines. In response, LG Electronics continues to develop innovations that place people at the centre of technology. Guided by its vision for smarter, more connected living, the company is introducing solutions that help consumers spend less time on household chores and more time on what matters most. Smarter Food Preservation for Modern Households Food remains at the heart of every home, making efficient food storage and preservation a priority for many families. Its spacious design also offers greater storage flexibility and easier organisation, helping families manage groceries more conveniently while maximising available space. item.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artist in Grammy History to Earn 100 Nominations!
item.description: Beyoncé becomes the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram If you have ever wondered what triple digits look like on music’s biggest stage, Beyoncé just gave everyone the answer. The Houston-born global music superstar has officially become the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations, hitting the milestone with her latest nod for “ Morning Dew ( Donk )”, which is nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards (2027 Grammys). Released in July 2026 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album B’Day, “Morning Dew (Donk)” puts her in a category alongside Kehlani , Victoria Monét , Jill Scott , and Nigerian star Tems . To put the 100-nomination milestone into perspective, no other recording artist has ever crossed into triple digits since the Grammys began. Beyoncé had previously been tied with her husband, Jay-Z , at 88 nominations each before breaking that tie in 2024 with 11 nods for Cowboy Carter to reach 99—and this latest recognition pushes her even further ahead as the artist with the highest number of Grammy nominations in history. Beyoncé holding her three Grammy trophies at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in 2025. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram It is also a good reminder of how long she has been doing this at the highest level. Beyoncé’s Grammy journey started all the way back in 2000 as part of Destiny’s Child with “Bills, Bills, Bills”, and across more than two decades as a solo artist, group member, and collaborator, she has built a record that keeps stretching further ahead of the pack. Alongside holding the title for the most Grammy nominations of all time, she is already the most awarded artist in Grammy history with 35 wins, a record she first broke in 2023 when she surpassed late conductor Georg Solti ’s 31 trophies. She pushed that tally even higher at the 2025 Grammys, taking home three awards—Album of the Year and Best Country Album for Cowboy Carter, as well as Best Country Duo/Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” alongside Miley Cyrus . Now all eyes turn to Sunday, 7 February 2027, when the 2027 Grammy Awards take place at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and we find out whether nomination number 100 turns into Grammy win number 36. item.title: From Bronze-Brown Traditional Attire to Bridal Lace, See Tomi Thomas & Efya’s Wedding Looks
item.description: Newlyweds Efya and Tomi Thomas at their white wedding reception in Accra. Photo Credit: Thret Studio/Instagram Two music stars, two countries, one beautiful love story! Nigerian singer Tomi Thomas and Ghanaian songstress Efya have made things official, celebrating their union in Accra with a wedding that brought Nigerian and Ghanaian traditions together. From their coordinated traditional looks to their elegant white wedding outfits and a song Tomi made especially for his bride, there was plenty to love about this celebration. If you’ve followed the music scenes in Nigeria and Ghana, you’ll know that Tomi and Efya have each carved out their own place in contemporary African music. Tomi Thomas, who hails from Delta State, Nigeria, first gained recognition as part of the music collective L.O.S (Loud On Sound), before building a solo catalogue that moves across Afro-fusion and alternative sounds. Efya, born Jane Awindor in Kumasi, Ghana, is one of the country’s most celebrated vocalists, known for her soulful music and multiple Ghana Music Awards. Now, the two have added a beautiful new chapter to their story, bringing their families, friends and two cultures together in Accra. Efya and Tomi Thomas in black and olive-green outfits for their wedding reception. Photo Credit: Photo Humor/Instagram One of the lovely fashion moments from the celebration was their Nigerian traditional attire. The couple coordinated in rich bronze-brown shades, with Tomi wearing a woven traditional robe, complete with a matching traditional cap. He accessorised with layered orange coral neck beads, matching wrist beads and black loafers, while carrying a circular feathered fan inscribed with “OGENEE”. Efya was every bit his match in a fitted, floor-length bronze-brown gown, with gold and silver beadwork covering the corset bodice and sheer sleeves. The structured peplum details at the hips added shape to the dress, while a beaded treble clef motif on the skirt made a sweet reference to the music that brought so much of their story together. She finished with a pleated gold-and-bronze headwrap, a white-and-coral beaded choker, coral earrings and gold strappy heels. Tomi Thomas and Efya in coordinated bronze-brown traditional attire for their wedding in Accra. Photo Credit: Tomi Thomas/Instagram For their white wedding, the couple opted for a timeless black-and-white palette. Tomi kept things classic in a double-breasted white tuxedo jacket, complete with a white pocket square, crisp dress shirt and black bow tie. Black tailored trousers and matching dress shoes completed his look. Efya, meanwhile, made a beautiful bridal entrance in a fitted white lace mermaid gown with an embellished illusion neckline, sheer floral lace long sleeves and a corset-style waist. The voluminous detachable overskirt added another dimension to the dress, while her sleek low bun and large white structured bouquet with a jewelled centre completed her bridal look. Group chats are buzzing, flights are being booked, wedding invitations are coming in, an everyone seems to have holiday plans. From concerts, parties, and social gatherings to family reunions and Christmas celebrations, there is always something happening. For many, it is the most anticipated time of the year, a chance to reconnect with loved ones, explore new places, and make the most of the holidays. For some, it’s the excitement of Detty December in Lagos. For others, it’s finally getting everyone together for Christmas, taking a much-needed break, or planning a getaway after a long year. With so much happening, one thing deserves a little more attention than it usually gets: where you’ll be staying. A good hotel can make all the difference to your holiday. Think relaxing mornings, comfortable rooms, good food, a convenient location, exciting experiences nearby, and somewhere to unwind after a long day of activities. After all, where you stay can shape your entire holiday experience. Whether you’re planning to experience Detty December in Lagos or spend Christmas in Enugu, we’ve put together a guide to some accommodation options and experiences worth considering as you plan your holiday. Where to Stay in Lagos for Detty December Anyone who has experienced Lagos in December knows that the city takes the festive season seriously. item.title: Tochukwu Ekoh: What My Friend’s Passing Taught Me About Kindness
item.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? What was the reason for that reconnection, and why did it have to end this way? The timing of certain events leaves you with more questions than answers. What makes this loss even more difficult to comprehend is how it happened. I had been the one who suffered an accident, yet I survived and was gradually recovering. He wasn’t sick. He hadn’t been involved in an accident. He simply slipped and fell, sustained an injury, and bled out. His body was not discovered until three days later. Three days. The loneliness he must have experienced within those three days, the possibility that he needed someone, and the heartbreaking thought that nobody knew what had happened to him. I cannot fully comprehend it. It also made me confront something I had perhaps never

item.title: Rema Reveals 7-Track E-Mortal Boy (EMB) EP Tracklist With Wizkid, BNYX & More
item.description: Rema preparing for the release of his new EP E-Mortal Boy following his singles TEA and Oh No. Come Friday, 20 November, seven brand-new tracks from Rema will be making their way to streaming platforms, and if the official tracklist for his upcoming EP, E-Mortal Boy ( EMB ), is anything to go by, Afrobeats listeners have quite a few new songs to look forward to over the weekend. First, the headline news everyone is talking about: Wizkid is on the opening track, “ Feel Alright “. This marks the very first time Rema and Wizkid have teamed up on an official joint song, which makes it an instant highlight before the rest of the EP even gets going. If you have already been replaying “ Oh No ” and “ TEA “, those two singles are right where they belong on the seven-song lineup, joined by two more solo records, “ VeLvet ” and “ SUGA “. Rema also brings in American producer BNYX or “ TANZANIA “, before wrapping things up on “ Bang Bang ” with longtime collaborator London and Nigerian-American singer Kah-Lo . Coming three years after his 2023 EP, Ravage, and two years after his Grammy-nominated sophomore album, HEIS, E-Mortal Boy ( EMB ) marks the Mavin Records and Jonzing World star’s next chapter—and Friday cannot come soon enough.
